docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4262:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:29:Method 4.2 extracts hidden states from Qwen3-VL-4B B1 runs and compares observation modes by layer. For each mode pair and layer, we compute the cosine gap between hidden-state means, evaluate AUROC by projecting examples onto the mean-difference direction, and summarize per-mode geometry through PCA top-10 variance. The classifieds baseline contains 288 examples, formed from 24 strong-tier tasks, two archived steps, and six modes, over 37 indexed layers.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4263:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:31:The robustness suite passes all five checks in the plan. Label permutation leaves the real AUROC 9.8 standard deviations above the permuted baseline. Per-task analysis is positive for all 24 tasks. Step 2 and step 5 curves are invariant at the mechanism level. The L23 silhouette score is at least 0.5, showing nontrivial clustering. Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals are tight, with widths of roughly 4-15% of the corresponding means.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4271:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:58:Activation patching provides the causal test. For each task, the clean/source run and corrupt/target run use the same archived browser step and deterministic 50-token continuation. In the core SoM-to-Phantom-SoM setup, the source prompt is `som`: task instruction, SoM prompt family, flat `[SOM_MARKS]` text, and annotated screenshot. The target prompt is `phantom_som`: the same instruction, same prompt family, and same `[SOM_MARKS]` text, but no image. Source hidden states are cached by layer, injected into the final input-token position of the target on the first forward pass, and subsequent decoding proceeds normally through the model cache.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4286:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:91:The format-variation grid contains ten modes: six marks-like variants, two controls, and DOM/SoM baselines. In the classifieds strong-tier baseline, all six marks-like variants peak at L36, the hash-ID control also peaks at L36, the plain-sentence control peaks at L17, and the DOM baseline preserves the L04 peak. Because L36 is the boundary layer, this is best read as a strong late/monotonic signature rather than as a precise late-layer mechanism.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4288:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:95:The reddit format run is cleaner for the mid-layer interpretation. Four of six marks-like variants peak at L17, the plain-sentence control peaks at L17, hash-ID control returns to L04, and DOM remains at L04. **W6 attribution** (`docs/checkpoints/mechanism/results/w6_h1_red_l04_attribution.md`, exploratory) further finds that the two L04 marks-like variants (`appagent_id`, `plain_numbered`) share a feature with the L04 DOM baseline: their first tokens are alphanumeric, while the four L17-peaking marks-like variants all start with markup-sigil tokens (`[`, `<`, `@`). The hash-ID control (`#a3f7`) starts with a sigil but lacks integer-marker structure and also peaks at L04, suggesting the trigger conjunction is integer-marker + markup-sigil rather than either alone. This is a post-hoc feature-attribution on a small (N=6 marks-like) format set; held-out falsifiers (`bare_N` = integer without sigil, `bracket_no_int` = sigil without integer) are not yet run. Cross-site, the safe claim is directional: marker formats that combine integer indexing with markup-sigil leading delimiters tend to delay image-axis separation into mid/late layers, while AXTree hierarchy and indexed-list variants lacking either feature preserve the early L04 image-axis peak. The reddit curve reveals the true L11-L17 fusion locus more clearly than the classifieds L36 boundary artifact.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4290:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:101:The second defense is selection-bias robustness. The classifieds reverse-tier run replicates the strong-tier H1 pattern, including L36 marks-like peaks and L04 DOM baseline. The shortcut signature is therefore not an artifact of selecting tasks where SoM beats DOM.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4292:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:105:The fourth defense is cross-site Mirage geometry. Reddit Method 4.2 reproduces the central relation: P-SoM is close to DOM/P-text at L17 and far from SoM/Vision on the image axis, with AUROC 1.0 on the key contrasts. This supports cross-site generalization of the mechanism claim, not B0/B1 capability scaling.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4305:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:133:Phantom-SoM's drop-one hero contribution in `fig_meta_forest.png` (reddit drop-one CI [+0.95, +6.19] strict-positive) therefore cannot be attributed to "three-axis positional uniqueness" with quantitatively distinct magnitudes. The cleaner mechanism story is: Phantom-SoM is one of four modes occupying the no-image-flat-marks half of the phantom routing space, all of which produce small geometric separation from each other; the behaviorally distinct success-task pool (Jaccard 0.29–0.49 against other arms) is what gives drop-one its complementarity, and patching displacement at L11–L17 shows the difference matters causally for token continuation. The bridge from patching displacement to behavioral SR remains open.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4308:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:139:Two corollaries follow. The mean hidden state at the final layer collapses to the shared JSON action-header tokens that every mode emits, so mode-distinct output signal is concentrated in the L23-L25 decoding window rather than at the final embedding. Whether the L23-L25 hidden representation can be used as a held-out mode classifier — with per-task AUROC, random-direction baseline, and competitive comparison to surface-token classifiers — is open work. Routing exploitation, deferred to paper 2, will need to make this case explicitly rather than inheriting it from §5.7.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/codex_stress_2026-05-13_wrap.md:4311:docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts/section5_mechanism.md:147:Literature positioning should stay modest. Section 5 applies the linear-readable, steerable, and mid/late-layer circuit framework to multimodal web-agent observation modes \citep{wu2026toolcalling,kaduri2024whatsintheimage,khorasani2026hdmi,fayyaz2026steermoe}. It should not claim novelty as the first such circuit or the first use of marked text. The contribution is controlled scientific characterization of the phantom boundary.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16036:+The default registry filter includes cells explicitly named `paper-grade-pre-bug`. Because `aggregate_phantom_lift.py`, `aggregate_routing_auroc.py`, figures, and status scripts use `get_cells()`/`get_run_dirs_paper_vwa()` without an explicit stricter grade, pre-bug data can enter primary §1/§4/§6 outputs by default. This is a config drift blocker, especially downstream of C10 gates and the B9 stale-claim precedent. Fix by making `paper-grade` the only default and requiring an explicit sensitivity flag for pre-bug cells.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16038:+### F02 — scripts/analysis/aggregate_phantom_lift.py:626 — BLOCKER
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16046:+If the registry yields no valid cells, the script still writes the primary `phantom_lift.csv`. Given the current manifest can intentionally archive cells, this can clobber the input to meta-analysis and figures while exiting normally. Paper-grade analysis should fail loudly when zero cells are eligible. Raise `SystemExit` before writing and print a manifest/skip diagnostic.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16048:+### F03 — scripts/analysis/aggregate_phantom_lift.py:209 — BLOCKER
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16055:+The function computes with `0.5pp`, but the same file later prints “TOST p ... at δ=1.0pp (commit-locked)” at line 665. This is a direct computation/prose contradiction for §4 phantom lift. Use a single constant, set it to the locked `1.0pp`, and reference that constant in the markdown. Cross-reference: this is the same stale-claim class as B9 `power_analysis.py`.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16057:+### F04 — scripts/analysis/aggregate_phantom_lift.py:231 — BLOCKER
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16064:+The prose says `p < alpha` rejects equivalence/nonzero, but for a clearly positive lift above `delta_pp`, `p_upper` approaches 1. This makes the reported TOST significance move opposite the substantive phantom-lift claim. Decide whether the test is equivalence (`|lift| < delta`) or practical nonzero (`lift > delta`) and compute the corresponding one-sided tail(s). Until fixed, TOST columns should not be used in paper text.

Since `load_per_cell_data()` does not carry `n_common`, tiny or partial cells can be pooled. Add `n_common` to the per-cell record and enforce the floor before `derslong_laird_meta()`. This affects §4 pooled phantom lift and the forest plots.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16162:+# directionality of "less than baseline" inverts. We flip sign of diff
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16174:+Activation patching exposes 36 transformer block hooks, not the 37 hidden-state sequence with embedding output used by `HiddenStateExtractor`. Downstream scripts and plots call layer 0 “embedding” and layer 35 “final baseline,” so the mechanism story can be mislabeled. Either include an embedding hook or relabel patch layers as block outputs. Cross-reference: this is the root cause for F12 and the G8 heterogeneity figure label drift.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16208:+        return (False, "eval_fp")
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16211:+The canonical FP filter expects exact eval-type strings. Runner and diagnostics construct composite strings such as `string_match|program_html`, so those rows do not match either branch. This under-filters `eval_fp` and directly corrupts §4 primary adjusted SR. Parse eval types as a list/set and use membership tests.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16233:+The fast path accepts any existing adjusted labels and does not validate `fp_reason`. A legacy row with `visual_fp` or another deprecated reason can bypass the §95 lock. Validate `fp_reason` against `{"", "na_fp", "eval_fp"}` and recompute/fail otherwise. This is the main FP consistency blocker.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16262:+Restart dedup depends entirely on a valid reset line with `step_idx == 0`. If the reset line is corrupt or a resumed retry starts at a nonzero step, old and new run fragments remain mixed. Add a run/session ID to step records or fail strict mode when dedup cannot prove one run. This is medium because the current runner usually starts at step 0.

The prose states a §6 comparative claim that the table does not test. Add explicit baseline comparison rows with uncertainty, or change the summary to “max signal per mode” only. This is a stale-claim risk for routing results.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16339:+This TOST is for relative cost equivalence, while the phantom-lift scripts discuss TOST for pp lift/equivalence/nonzero. The shared name and `TOST_delta=1.0` CLI wording can confuse prereg decisions. Rename this to `evaluate_cost_tost` and keep lift TOST separate. This is a medium stale-method risk.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16489:+The default registry filter includes cells explicitly named `paper-grade-pre-bug`. Because `aggregate_phantom_lift.py`, `aggregate_routing_auroc.py`, figures, and status scripts use `get_cells()`/`get_run_dirs_paper_vwa()` without an explicit stricter grade, pre-bug data can enter primary §1/§4/§6 outputs by default. This is a config drift blocker, especially downstream of C10 gates and the B9 stale-claim precedent. Fix by making `paper-grade` the only default and requiring an explicit sensitivity flag for pre-bug cells.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16491:+### F02 — scripts/analysis/aggregate_phantom_lift.py:626 — BLOCKER
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16499:+If the registry yields no valid cells, the script still writes the primary `phantom_lift.csv`. Given the current manifest can intentionally archive cells, this can clobber the input to meta-analysis and figures while exiting normally. Paper-grade analysis should fail loudly when zero cells are eligible. Raise `SystemExit` before writing and print a manifest/skip diagnostic.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16501:+### F03 — scripts/analysis/aggregate_phantom_lift.py:209 — BLOCKER
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16508:+The function computes with `0.5pp`, but the same file later prints “TOST p ... at δ=1.0pp (commit-locked)” at line 665. This is a direct computation/prose contradiction for §4 phantom lift. Use a single constant, set it to the locked `1.0pp`, and reference that constant in the markdown. Cross-reference: this is the same stale-claim class as B9 `power_analysis.py`.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16510:+### F04 — scripts/analysis/aggregate_phantom_lift.py:231 — BLOCKER
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16517:+The prose says `p < alpha` rejects equivalence/nonzero, but for a clearly positive lift above `delta_pp`, `p_upper` approaches 1. This makes the reported TOST significance move opposite the substantive phantom-lift claim. Decide whether the test is equivalence (`|lift| < delta`) or practical nonzero (`lift > delta`) and compute the corresponding one-sided tail(s). Until fixed, TOST columns should not be used in paper text.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16519:+### F05 — scripts/analysis/aggregate_phantom_lift.py:94 — HIGH

Since `load_per_cell_data()` does not carry `n_common`, tiny or partial cells can be pooled. Add `n_common` to the per-cell record and enforce the floor before `derslong_laird_meta()`. This affects §4 pooled phantom lift and the forest plots.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16615:+# directionality of "less than baseline" inverts. We flip sign of diff
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16627:+Activation patching exposes 36 transformer block hooks, not the 37 hidden-state sequence with embedding output used by `HiddenStateExtractor`. Downstream scripts and plots call layer 0 “embedding” and layer 35 “final baseline,” so the mechanism story can be mislabeled. Either include an embedding hook or relabel patch layers as block outputs. Cross-reference: this is the root cause for F12 and the G8 heterogeneity figure label drift.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16661:+        return (False, "eval_fp")
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16664:+The canonical FP filter expects exact eval-type strings. Runner and diagnostics construct composite strings such as `string_match|program_html`, so those rows do not match either branch. This under-filters `eval_fp` and directly corrupts §4 primary adjusted SR. Parse eval types as a list/set and use membership tests.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16686:+The fast path accepts any existing adjusted labels and does not validate `fp_reason`. A legacy row with `visual_fp` or another deprecated reason can bypass the §95 lock. Validate `fp_reason` against `{"", "na_fp", "eval_fp"}` and recompute/fail otherwise. This is the main FP consistency blocker.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16715:+Restart dedup depends entirely on a valid reset line with `step_idx == 0`. If the reset line is corrupt or a resumed retry starts at a nonzero step, old and new run fragments remain mixed. Add a run/session ID to step records or fail strict mode when dedup cannot prove one run. This is medium because the current runner usually starts at step 0.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16771:+    "# Routing signal AUROC summary — max per (baseline, site, mode)",
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16773:+    "Section 6 claim: AUROC ≥ baseline (DOM/SoM/Vision) for Phantom modes.",
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16775:+The script reports the maximum AUROC within each mode but never computes phantom-vs-baseline contrasts. The prose states a §6 comparative claim that the table does not test. Add explicit baseline comparison rows with uncertainty, or change the summary to “max signal per mode” only. This is a stale-claim risk for routing results.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16792:+This TOST is for relative cost equivalence, while the phantom-lift scripts discuss TOST for pp lift/equivalence/nonzero. The shared name and `TOST_delta=1.0` CLI wording can confuse prereg decisions. Rename this to `evaluate_cost_tost` and keep lift TOST separate. This is a medium stale-method risk.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16814:+### F36 — scripts/maintenance/glm/myriad_watcher.py:96 — HIGH
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16821:+The watcher intentionally exits success on SSH/qstat failure. Transient silence is acceptable once, but repeated failures hide job states and failed reruns. Persist a failure counter and notify after a threshold. For paper-grade cron, repeated watcher failure should be visible.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:16831:+The pre-launch GLM gate allows launch when the review call fails. Return WARN/BLOCK on GLM failure for paper-grade launches unless an explicit override is supplied.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17083:+# directionality of "less than baseline" inverts. We flip sign of diff
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17095:+Activation patching exposes 36 transformer block hooks, not the 37 hidden-state sequence with embedding output used by `HiddenStateExtractor`. Downstream scripts and plots call layer 0 “embedding” and layer 35 “final baseline,” so the mechanism story can be mislabeled. Either include an embedding hook or relabel patch layers as block outputs. Cross-reference: this is the root cause for F12 and the G8 heterogeneity figure label drift.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17129:+        return (False, "eval_fp")
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17132:+The canonical FP filter expects exact eval-type strings. Runner and diagnostics construct composite strings such as `string_match|program_html`, so those rows do not match either branch. This under-filters `eval_fp` and directly corrupts §4 primary adjusted SR. Parse eval types as a list/set and use membership tests.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17154:+The fast path accepts any existing adjusted labels and does not validate `fp_reason`. A legacy row with `visual_fp` or another deprecated reason can bypass the §95 lock. Validate `fp_reason` against `{"", "na_fp", "eval_fp"}` and recompute/fail otherwise. This is the main FP consistency blocker.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17183:+Restart dedup depends entirely on a valid reset line with `step_idx == 0`. If the reset line is corrupt or a resumed retry starts at a nonzero step, old and new run fragments remain mixed. Add a run/session ID to step records or fail strict mode when dedup cannot prove one run. This is medium because the current runner usually starts at step 0.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17239:+    "# Routing signal AUROC summary — max per (baseline, site, mode)",
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17241:+    "Section 6 claim: AUROC ≥ baseline (DOM/SoM/Vision) for Phantom modes.",
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17243:+The script reports the maximum AUROC within each mode but never computes phantom-vs-baseline contrasts. The prose states a §6 comparative claim that the table does not test. Add explicit baseline comparison rows with uncertainty, or change the summary to “max signal per mode” only. This is a stale-claim risk for routing results.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17260:+This TOST is for relative cost equivalence, while the phantom-lift scripts discuss TOST for pp lift/equivalence/nonzero. The shared name and `TOST_delta=1.0` CLI wording can confuse prereg decisions. Rename this to `evaluate_cost_tost` and keep lift TOST separate. This is a medium stale-method risk.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17289:+The watcher intentionally exits success on SSH/qstat failure. Transient silence is acceptable once, but repeated failures hide job states and failed reruns. Persist a failure counter and notify after a threshold. For paper-grade cron, repeated watcher failure should be visible.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17299:+The pre-launch GLM gate allows launch when the review call fails. Return WARN/BLOCK on GLM failure for paper-grade launches unless an explicit override is supplied.

docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17414:+The default registry filter includes cells explicitly named `paper-grade-pre-bug`. Because `aggregate_phantom_lift.py`, `aggregate_routing_auroc.py`, figures, and status scripts use `get_cells()`/`get_run_dirs_paper_vwa()` without an explicit stricter grade, pre-bug data can enter primary §1/§4/§6 outputs by default. This is a config drift blocker, especially downstream of C10 gates and the B9 stale-claim precedent. Fix by making `paper-grade` the only default and requiring an explicit sensitivity flag for pre-bug cells.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17416:+### F02 — scripts/analysis/aggregate_phantom_lift.py:626 — BLOCKER
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17424:+If the registry yields no valid cells, the script still writes the primary `phantom_lift.csv`. Given the current manifest can intentionally archive cells, this can clobber the input to meta-analysis and figures while exiting normally. Paper-grade analysis should fail loudly when zero cells are eligible. Raise `SystemExit` before writing and print a manifest/skip diagnostic.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17426:+### F03 — scripts/analysis/aggregate_phantom_lift.py:209 — BLOCKER
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17433:+The function computes with `0.5pp`, but the same file later prints “TOST p ... at δ=1.0pp (commit-locked)” at line 665. This is a direct computation/prose contradiction for §4 phantom lift. Use a single constant, set it to the locked `1.0pp`, and reference that constant in the markdown. Cross-reference: this is the same stale-claim class as B9 `power_analysis.py`.
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17435:+### F04 — scripts/analysis/aggregate_phantom_lift.py:231 — BLOCKER
docs/checkpoints/codex_outputs/code_audit_2026-05-09_run.log:17442:+The prose says `p < alpha` rejects equivalence/nonzero, but for a clearly positive lift above `delta_pp`, `p_upper` approaches 1. This makes the reported TOST significance move opposite the substantive phantom-lift claim. Decide whether the test is equivalence (`|lift| < delta`) or practical nonzero (`lift > delta`) and compute the corresponding one-sided tail(s). Until fixed, TOST columns should not be used in paper text.

    27	
    28	This pre-registration adopts a **Hero + Drop-in + Structural + Framing-Rule** hierarchy rather than the more conventional "all hypotheses pre-committed strict" pattern. The rationale (developed via 2026-05-03 design discussion):
    29	
    30	1. **Phantom-SoM is the deployment hero**: 4-fold drop-in property (cost ≈ DOM, latency ~50% lower, signal AUROC ≥ baseline, drop-one positive) is the headline practical contribution. This is pre-registered strict.
    31

   231	### §5.X Post-hoc Layer Selection Disclosure (Stage 2 Mechanism, audit G5)
   232	
   233	Stage 2 mechanistic activation patching identified mid-layer disruption peaking
   234	at **L17** (3 of 4 cells Holm-significant on `token_overlap_to_target`, p_Holm <
   235	0.05; cell D L11+L17 strongest p_Holm = 0.006/0.008 \*\*). The L11/L17 layer
   236	selection has the following **explicit pre-vs-post-hoc structure**:
   237	
   238	| Stage | Layer rationale | Status |
   239	|---|---|---|
   240	| **Stage 2A logit_shift pilot** (5-task aggregate, 笔记 §111.5) | L17 emerged as peak in independent `logit_shift` metric | **Hypothesis-generating** — first-pass discovery |
   241	| **§111 task-0 single-task patching** | L11 flipped 93% match in N=1 task | **Hypothesis-generating** — distribution outlier (acknowledged 笔记 §117.4) |
   242	| **Stage 2B 24-task aggregate (cell A)** | L17 Holm-significant (p_Holm = 0.011 \*\*) — confirmed Stage 2A peak | **Confirmatory** — independent metric agreement |
   243	| **Stage 2C reverse 15-task (cell B)** | L11 + L17 Holm-significant — direction-paired confirmation | **Confirmatory** |
   244	| **Cell D (rev × strong-tier 24)** | L11 + L17 strongest (p_Holm = 0.006/0.008 \*\*) | **Confirmatory** — cross-tier replication |
   245	
   246	**Disclosure**: Layers L11 and L17 were not pre-registered before Stage 2 data
   247	collection; they emerged from Stage 2A pilot (the *hypothesis-generating* phase)
   248	and were confirmed by Stage 2B/2C scaled-up data (the *confirmatory* phase). To
   249	mitigate the multiple-comparison concern, all per-direction tests use Holm-
   250	Bonferroni correction across the canonical layer grid (L0/5/11/17/23/29 vs L35
   251	baseline) — this catches the "any layer might pop" multiple-testing concern.
   252	
   253	**Reviewer-defense**: We do NOT claim pre-registered layer prediction. We claim
   254	that the **same** mid-layer region (L11-L17) emerges across (a) Stage 2A
   255	logit_shift, (b) Stage 2B forward overlap-to-target, (c) Stage 2C reverse,
   256	(d) Cell D cross-tier rev-on-strong. Convergence across 4 independent analysis
   257	paths constitutes confirmatory evidence even without pre-registered layer
   258	prediction. Cell E random-injection control (G6) further demonstrates content-
   259	specificity, ruling out generic-injection alternative explanations.

    97	
    98	Drop to `paper-grade-pre-bug` if any of those conditions weren't met,
    99	or for the legacy 2026-04 cells.
   100	
   101	### Verify after launch
   102	
   103	```bash
   104	.venv/bin/python3 -c "
   105	from scripts.analysis.lib.run_registry import get_cells
   106	print(get_cells(baseline='B0', site='reddit', mode='phantom_som'))
   107	"
   108	# Should print [CellSpec(...)]; if empty, manifest update missed.
   109	```
   110	
   111	---
   112	
   113	## 2. The launch command (per cell)
   114	
   115	Pre-flight done + manifest entry added → run:
   116	
   117	```bash
   118	make launch BASELINE=B0 SITE=reddit MODE=phantom_som
   119	```
   120	
   121	What `launch.sh` does (audit-traced flow):
   122	
   123	1. **Auto-create cell-md** at `_status/cells/cell_b0_red_psom.md` (if
   124	   missing) with frontmatter `status: pending`.
   125	2. **`make pre-launch-check`** (C10 + F audit):
   126	   - Git working tree clean (no untracked, no diff).
   127	   - VWA submodule SHA = lock.
   128	   - HF Qwen3-VL-4B revision present.
   129	   - Playwright 1.58.0.
   130	   - Disk free > 20 GB.
   131	   - Seed = 42 in base config.
   132	   - **pytest passes (60s timeout, fail-fast)** ← audit F.
   133	3. **`glm_pre_launch_check.py`**: GLM reads queue script + active
   134	   processes + recent logs. rc=2 BLOCK abort / rc=1 WARN interactive
   135	   y/N / rc=0 OK. Fail-closed when GLM unreachable (audit F37); set
   136	   `P79_ALLOW_GLM_FAIL=1` only for dev runs.
   137	4. **`nohup queue_phantom_som.sh B0 reddit`** in background with
   138	   `RESET_BEFORE=1`. PID printed.
   139	5. **30-second post-hook**: dual GLM refresh
   140	   (`glm-update-cells` + `glm-refresh-playbook`) so PLAYBOOK §1
   141	   narrative reflects the new run within ~30 seconds.
   142	
   143	---
   144	
   145	## 3. During the run (continuous monitoring)
   146	
   147	| Frequency | What | Where |
   148	|---|---|---|
   149	| Real-time | Active processes + episode mtime | `make active` |
   150	| Every 5 min | Errors / OOM / NOT_LOGGED_IN / Magento 302 / cutlass / sm_121 / fp_adjust_error | cron `error-scan` → PLAYBOOK §2.5 |
   151	| Every 5 min | Disk free + Tailscale BackendState (audit E) | `error_scan.json system_health` |
   152	| Every 5 min | Myriad qstat + state diff (if Stage 2 cells running) | cron `myriad-watcher` |
   153	| Every 10 min | Cell frontmatter sync (progress / pid / sr_raw / history) | cron `glm-update-cells` |
   154	| Every 30 min | PLAYBOOK §2 fast refresh (cron health + dead-links + ntfy fails) | cron `glm-refresh-playbook-s2` |
   155	| Every 2 hours | PLAYBOOK §1 narrative + §2 board | cron `glm-refresh-playbook` |
   156	| Continuous | REPORT / IDLE / SESSION-HEALTH watchdog | runner-paired `experiment_watchdog.py` |
   157	
   158	### When to expect an alert
   159	
   160	Single ntfy topic: `p79-exp-dgx-spark`. Alerts:
   161	
   162	- **High priority**: IDLE (no episode in N min), 3-consec SSH chain
   163	  fail (F36), 3-consec GLM API fail (audit D), disk free <50 GB
   164	  (E), tailscale non-running (E), 0-files SCP failure (auto_pull
   165	  audit A), watchdog auth refresh failed.
   166	- **Default priority**: per-condition COMPLETE, Myriad state changes
   167	  (NEW/CHG/GONE), per-cell auto_pull complete.
   168	
   169	### When to act manually
   170	
   171	| Symptom | Action |
   172	|---|---|
   173	| 3 consec NOT_LOGGED_IN despite watchdog auth refresh | Quark side: re-launch Docker reddit/cls/shop containers; re-export auth via Playwright record |
   174	| Disk free crashing | Prune `logs/B0_*.log` (>30 days), archive `results/visualwebarena/phase1/<old_run>/artifacts/` to S3 |
   175	| Myriad SSH chain dead 30 min+ | Quark side: reconnect Cisco AnyConnect; check `tailscale status` |
   176	| Cell quarantined (audit C validate-strict fail) | Inspect `validation_report.json`; common: missing summary fields, low SR vs prior cell, unexpected fp_reason |
   177	
   178	---
   179	
   180	## 4. Per-cell completion (autonomous, audit B chain)
   181	
   182	When a cell's runner finishes (episodes ≥ expected_n):
   183	
   184	1. **`glm-update-cells` cron** (next 10-min tick) detects active→done
   185	   flip → frontmatter `status: done`, `finalized_at`, history append.
   186	2. **Audit B trigger**: `nohup make analysis FAST=1 &` fires →
   187	   aggregator (`aggregate_phantom_lift.py` + `aggregate_phantom_meta.py`
   188	   + `sr_fp_per_mode.py`) + figures regen. Logged to
   189	   `logs/cron/post_finalize_analysis.log`.
   190	3. **Manual brain decision** (NOT automated):
   191	   - Append `实验笔记.md §X` chronicle entry with finding (`#finding`).
   192	   - Update `paper_planning.md §3` if cross-X pattern emerges.
   193	   - Update `paper_drafts/` if section-level prose needs revision.
   194	
   195	For Stage 2 mechanism cells (Myriad-launched):
   196	
   197	1. **Myriad job finishes** (state r → gone in `qstat`).
   198	2. Cron `myriad-watcher` (next 5-min tick) detects GONE event →
   199	   ntfy + dispatches `auto_pull_myriad_cell.sh` (audit A).
   200	3. **Auto-pull script**: SCP via SSH chain → `validate_run.py
   201	   --strict` → cell-md frontmatter update (`quarantined` if validate
   202	   fails) → `make analysis FAST=1` → ntfy "Cell pulled".
   203	
   204	---
   205	
   206	## 5. Post-batch (after all 16 cells done)
   207	
   208	- [ ] All 16 cell-md `status: done` (none `quarantined`):
   209	      ```bash
   210	      grep -l "status: quarantined" docs/checkpoints/_status/cells/cell_*.md
   211	      ```
   212	      If any quarantined: investigate `validation_report.json`, fix
   213	      bug, re-launch with explicit `RESET=1`.
   214	- [ ] **`make analysis`** (full, not FAST=1) regenerates all
   215	      aggregators + figures. Should produce **paper-grade** numbers
   216	      (not pre-bug; the F01 + F40 chain enforces this).
   217	- [ ] **`scripts/analysis/sensitivity_loo_meta.py`**: re-run; verify
   218	      P-text drop-in arm robustness post-rerun (was FRAGILE on 3 cells;
   219	      may stabilize on 16).
   220	- [ ] **`scripts/analysis/power_analysis.py`** with observed SR:
   221	      regenerate `docs/analysis/cross_sites/power_analysis.md`.
   222	- [ ] **Update `section8_limitations.md`** §8.5 + §8.6 with final
   223	      numbers (mechanism cells F/G results + sparse-mechanism caveat
   224	      reaffirmed).
   225	- [ ] Append `实验笔记.md §X` chronicle: full 16-cell summary.
   226	- [ ] **Push 16-cell rerun commit batch** + tag `paper-grade-rerun-<date>`.
   227	
   228	---
   229	
   230	## 6. Rollback / abort
   231	
   232	If contamination detected mid-batch (cross-baseline same site, auth
   233	drift not auto-recovered, etc.):
   234	
   235	```bash
   236	# 1. Kill runner + watchdog cleanly:
   237	pgrep -af "run_experiment.*<SITE>" | awk '{print $1}' | xargs kill -TERM
   238	
   239	# 2. Mark cell as dirty:
   240	.venv/bin/python3 scripts/maintenance/mark_cell_dirty.py \
   241	    --cell docs/checkpoints/_status/cells/cell_<id>.md \
   242	    --reason "contamination" --commit-sha $(git rev-parse HEAD)
   243	
   244	# 3. Reset site:
   245	RESET_BEFORE=1 bash scripts/maintenance/reset_vwa_sites.sh <SITE>
   246	
   247	# 4. Update manifest entry: grade: archived → keep history; or remove
   248	#    entirely if never paper-grade.
   249	
   250	# 5. Re-launch with fresh queue (skip-restart guard cleared):
   251	make launch BASELINE=<bx> SITE=<sx> MODE=<mx> FORCE_RESTART=1
   252	```
   253	
   254	---
   255	
   256	## Quick reference
   257	
   258	```bash
   259	# Pre-flight
   260	make pre-launch-check                              # programmatic gates
   261	git pull && git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all   # clean tree
   262	
   263	# Manifest update
   264	$EDITOR results/phantom_paper/run_manifest.yaml
   265	
   266	# Launch
   267	make launch BASELINE=B0 SITE=reddit MODE=phantom_som
   268	
   269	# Monitor
   270	make active                                        # real-time
   271	tail -f logs/cron/error_scan.log                   # 5min
   272	ntfy.sh/p79-exp-dgx-spark                          # phone
   273	
   274	# Post-cell
   275	# (audit B chain auto-fires; if needed:)
   276	make analysis FAST=1
   277	
   278	# Post-batch
   279	make analysis                                      # full
   280	.venv/bin/python3 scripts/analysis/sensitivity_loo_meta.py
   281	.venv/bin/python3 scripts/analysis/power_analysis.py --baseline-sr <observed>
   282	```
   283	
   284	---
   285	
   286	## Audit B/C/D/E/F/G chain in this checklist
   287	
   288	- **A** (auto-pull) → §4 Stage 2 mechanism cells
   289	- **B** (analysis trigger on done) → §4 per-cell completion
   290	- **C** (validate-strict gate) → §4 + §5 quarantine handling
   291	- **D** (GLM fail counter) → §3 high-priority alerts
   292	- **E** (disk + tailscale) → §0 pre-flight + §3 alert table
   293	- **F** (pytest gate) → §2 launch command flow
   294	- **G** (P79-specific patterns) → §3 error monitoring
   295	
   296	Open follow-ups (not in (A)-(G)):
   297	- **H** A1 prereg lock enforcement in `make pre-launch-check` (currently §0 manual check)
   298	- **I** weekly artifacts prune cron
   299	- **J** weekly ntfy heartbeat

## docs/checkpoints/pre_run/dataset_card.md
     1	# Dataset Card
     2	
     3	> Per Gebru et al. 2018 "Datasheets for Datasets". Addresses audit
     4	> constraint **A13** (datasheet-style disclosure for benchmark composition).
     5	
     6	## Benchmark identity
     7	
     8	| Field | Value |
     9	|---|---|
    10	| Name | **VisualWebArena (VWA)** |
    11	| Citation | Koh et al. 2024 (`paper.bib` `koh2024visualwebarena`) |
    12	| Repo | https://github.com/web-arena-x/visualwebarena |
    13	| Submodule SHA in this work | **`832f037e2cc7ebda4a41831443a3fc9b79d06cd6`** (per `locked_versions.md`) |
    14	| License | Apache 2.0 |
    15	
    16	## Sites in scope
    17	
    18	This paper uses **3 of 3** VWA sites. All sites are self-hosted Docker
    19	containers (no external HTTP traffic to commercial sites — paper-grade
    20	privacy + reproducibility).
    21	
    22	| Site | N tasks | Task-pool sha256 | Site type | Hosted at |
    23	|---|---|---|---|---|
    24	| **classifieds** | 234 | `d36a20c1eaa1f5da...` | Visual-rich product listings (Magento-based) | DGX Tailscale → quark Docker container `:9980` (cf. `memory/MEMORY.md` "Docker 容器端口") |
    25	| **reddit** | 210 | `ecd4ed4370740fd6...` | Text-dominated forum threads (Postmill) | DGX Tailscale → quark `:9999` |
    26	| **shopping** | 466 | `07889e3646ee10e3...` | Mixed text + image product pages (Magento) | DGX Tailscale → quark `:7770` |
    27	| **Total** | **910** | — | | |
    28	
    29	WebArena (480 tasks across shopping/shopping_admin/reddit) is **out of scope**
    30	for this paper per `preregistration.md §7` external validity scope. Cross-bench
    31	generalization is explicit future work.
    32	
    33	## Task curation methodology
    34	
    35	### Inclusion
    36	
    37	All 910 VWA tasks are **included by default** in the locked 16-cell rerun
    38	(per `preregistration.md §4` cell inclusion criteria):
    39	
    40	- Phase A post-fix code only (commit ≥ `3c15cd7`)
    41	- Per-cell N inclusion floor ≥ 100 episodes
    42	- All locked modes per cell (DOM / SoM / Vision / phantom_som / phantom_dom
    43	  for B0/B1, plus phantom_text / phantom_prompt for select cells)
    44	
    45	### Exclusion (post-FP-filter)
    46	
    47	Per `preregistration.md §4` FP filter primary spec (`na_fp + eval_fp` combined),
    48	per-task exclusions are:
    49	
    50	| Filter | What it excludes | Rationale | Audited at |
    51	|---|---|---|---|
    52	| `na_fp` | Tasks marked N/A by ground truth where agent emitted `finish.answer="X"` (non-N/A) and was scored success by mistake | Mirage prevention; agent overconfidence on impossible tasks should not be rewarded | 笔记 §78a |
    53	| `eval_fp` | Tasks where evaluator's program_html / string_match scoring is logged as ambiguous-pass (e.g., URL prefix match where agent navigated past target) | Evaluator-reliability defense | 笔记 §95 |
    54	| `visual_fp` | **DEPRECATED** — boundary-undecidable, over-filters 95.3% VWA tasks | Removed per evaluator change protocol T2 simplification | `evaluator_change_protocol.md §7` |
    55	
    56	### Robustness sensitivity
    57	
    58	Per `preregistration.md §4` FP filter sensitivity ladder, **3 variants reported**
    59	in paper appendix:
    60	
    61	1. `raw_SR` (no FP filter)
    62	2. `+na_fp only` (just N/A exclusion)
    63	3. `+na_fp+eval_fp combined` (primary)
    64	
    65	H1/H3 conclusions must hold under all 3 variants (paper §3 sensitivity disclosure).
    66	
    67	### Manual non-visual subset (Appendix D robustness)
    68	
    69	Replaces deprecated `visual_fp` with **manually-audited 43 VWA + 480 WA = 523
    70	non-visual tasks** (`docs/analysis/cross_sites/vwa_manual_non_visual_task_ids.py`).
    71	Used as Appendix D robustness check to confirm paper §1 hero finding holds
    72	on tasks where image is not necessary (rules out "phantom modes work because
    73	target tasks don't need image" trivial alternative).
    74	
    75	## Per-site task characteristics
    76	
    77	### classifieds (visual-rich)
    78	
    79	- Product listings with thumbnails, prices, location, category breadcrumbs
    80	- 234 tasks, N/A rate ~5-8%, image visibility critical for ~60-70% of tasks
    81	- SR pattern (per `section1_intro.md`): full SoM **21.37%** > Phantom-SoM **14.53%** (image-grounded advantage clear)
    82	- Common failure modes: visual hijack (B1 70.4%), early finish on stale page (B0 53.3%)
    83	
    84	### reddit (text-dominated)
    85	
    86	- Forum threads with text posts, comments, upvote counts; image attachments occasional
    87	- 210 tasks, N/A rate ~10-12%, image visibility critical for ~30-40% of tasks
    88	- SR pattern: Phantom-SoM **13.81%** ≈ full SoM **10.48%** (text-only modes competitive)
    89	- Common failure modes: navigate-to-comments confusion, comment-vs-post target ambiguity
    90	
    91	### shopping (mixed)
    92	
    93	- Product detail pages, search results, cart pages
    94	- 466 tasks (largest), N/A rate ~6-9%, image visibility critical for ~50% of tasks
    95	- Pilot pending (currently DOM-only B0 cls + B1 cls done; full 5-mode shop in 16-cell rerun)
    96	- Expected SR pattern: similar to classifieds (visual-rich) but more text-rich than classifieds
    97	
    98	## Auxiliary images
    99	
   100	Some VWA tasks reference images via `[Input image 1]` placeholders in prompts.
   101	These are loaded from `external/visualwebarena/config_files/vwa/<site>/`
   102	and hashed per-image into `env_snapshot.json` `extra.reference_images_sha256`
   103	per run, ensuring byte-identical reference imagery across reruns.
   104	
   105	## Data sharing & redaction
   106	
   107	The released artifact (per `preregistration.md §7` reproducibility scope) includes:
   108	
   109	- **Task config files** (full 910 task pool): MIT license inherited from VWA
   110	- **Curated mirage subset** (`results/mechanistic/archive_subset_b1_{cls,reddit}/`):
   111	  47-48 + 24-15 task subsets with cached observations + `screenshot_annotated.png`
   112	- **Run artifacts** (per-cell episode JSONLs, summaries, env_snapshots): paper-grade
   113	
   114	Excluded from release:
   115	- VWA Docker images (replicators pull from VWA repo themselves)
   116	- Site auth state (`.auth/`, gitignored — synthetic seed users only, no real user data)
   117	- B0 proxy API credentials
   118	
   119	## Privacy & ethics
   120	
   121	VWA tasks are **synthetic**. The Docker containers host:
   122	
   123	- Synthetic seed accounts: `emma.lopez` (shopping), `MarvelsGrantMan136` (reddit), `blake.sullivan` (classifieds) — generated by VWA team, no real user data
   124	- Synthetic content: catalog, posts, listings — none reference real people or real-world events
   125	- No PII, no real transactions, no scraped real user data
   126	
   127	IRB review **not required** per `pre_run/ethics_license_coi_statements.md`.
   128	
   129	## Known issues / caveats
   130	
   131	| Issue | Catalog ID | Status |
   132	|---|---|---|
   133	| `ua_match` GPT-4o-mini judge drift | `master_bug_catalog.md` B-20 | DISCLOSED — temperature=0 pin + na_fp class |
   134	| `string_match fuzzy_threshold` only honors 1.0 | B-21 | DISCLOSED — fixed at 1.0 across all conditions |
   135	| VWA site state contamination (cart/listing accumulation) | `experiment_launch_rules.md` | MITIGATED — `RESET_BEFORE=1` protocol per cell |
   136	| Reference image loading bug pre-Phase-A | B-36 | FIXED — Phase A post-fix `3c15cd7+` |
   137	
   138	## Per-task ID stability
   139	
   140	`(benchmark, site, task_id)` triple is the canonical unique key per
   141	`master_bug_catalog.md` B-80. Cross-benchmark task IDs cannot collide
   142	because benchmark / site is explicit in manifests.
   143	
   144	## References
   145	
   146	- Gebru et al. 2018 "Datasheets for Datasets" (NEEDS_BIB_ENTRY)
   147	- `paper.bib` `koh2024visualwebarena` (VWA itself)
   148	- `pre_run/locked_versions.md` for VWA SHA + per-site task-pool hashes
   149	- `pre_run/preregistration.md §4` for FP filter + cell inclusion locks
   150	- `master_bug_catalog.md` for known evaluator issues

## docs/checkpoints/pre_run/model_card.md
     1	# Model Card
     2	
     3	> Per Mitchell et al. 2019 "Model Cards for Model Reporting". Addresses
     4	> audit constraint **A12** (model-card-like disclosure for B0/B1 model
     5	> identity, access, decoding, and limitations).
     6	
     7	This paper studies two web-agent baselines, **B0** and **B1**. Below are
     8	their full identity / capability / limitation cards.
     9	
    10	---
    11	
    12	## B0 — Qwen3-Omni-235B-Thinking (proxy API)
    13	
    14	### Identity
    15	
    16	| Field | Value |
    17	|---|---|
    18	| Provider | HolisticAI internal proxy → upstream Qwen API |
    19	| Model name | `qwen3-omni-235b-thinking` |
    20	| Architecture | Mixture-of-Experts (235B total params, ~22B active) |
    21	| Modality | Multimodal: text, image, audio (we use text + image only) |
    22	| Access | Closed-weight, API-only via HolisticAI proxy at `${PROXY_BASE_URL}` (gitignored) |
    23	| Authentication | `${PROXY_API_KEY}` env var, sourced from `.env` (gitignored) |
    24	| Cost (per token) | Subsidized by HolisticAI lab budget; replicators with separate Qwen API access pay vendor rates |
    25	
    26	### Decoding
    27	
    28	| Parameter | Value |
    29	|---|---|
    30	| Temperature | **0.0** (greedy server-side decoding) |
    31	| max_tokens | per-task, default 4096 |
    32	| Top-p / top-k | not used (temperature=0 → deterministic) |
    33	| Stop tokens | per-task config, including `</finish>` |
    34	| Server-side determinism | **best-effort**: API providers don't strictly guarantee bitwise determinism even at temperature=0 (load-balancing across model replicas, MoE routing variance, kernel selection may introduce <1‰ output drift). Reported as "one controlled stochastic sample" with task-level bootstrap uncertainty per `preregistration.md §7`. |
    35	
    36	### Capability profile (intended use)
    37	
    38	- Web-agent multi-step reasoning over DOM / SoM / Vision observations
    39	- VWA classifieds / reddit / shopping (910 tasks across 3 sites in scope)
    40	- 2-step lookahead reasoning for action selection
    41	- N/A task detection (terminating with `finish.answer="N/A"` when site contains no valid candidate)
    42	
    43	### Limitations
    44	
    45	- **Stochasticity**: server-side may drift on identical input (see decoding above)
    46	- **Action grammar**: VWA verbose action format; agent occasionally emits malformed action JSON requiring fallback to no-op
    47	- **No system role**: paper-grade convention uses user-role-only chat template (`memory/MEMORY.md` guard rail) — preserves hundreds of episode comparison consistency
    48	- **Cost asymmetry vs B1**: B0 is API-only, scales with usage; B1 is fully local. Asymmetry disclosed as design constraint per `paper_planning.md` and `preregistration.md` (no remediation, intended scientific design)
    49	- **Closed weights**: cannot probe internals (logits / attention / hidden states); SteerMoE-style mechanism analysis deferred to future work (see `negative_results_registry.md` entry #9)
    50	- **Proxy availability**: API endpoint may degrade or sunset post-publication; replicators verify via released traces (`preregistration.md §7` reproducibility tier)
    51	
    52	---
    53	
    54	## B1 — Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (local)
    55	
    56	### Identity
    57	
    58	| Field | Value |
    59	|---|---|
    60	| Provider | Alibaba (Qwen team) |
    61	| Model name | `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` |
    62	| HuggingFace revision SHA | **`ebb281ec70b05090aa6165b016eac8ec08e71b17`** (pinned, see `locked_versions.md`) |
    63	| Architecture | Dense decoder-only transformer (4B params) + vision encoder (~700M params for image embedding) |
    64	| Modality | Multimodal text + image (used for both VWA agent + Stage 2 mechanistic analysis) |
    65	| Access | **Open weights** — fully reproducible, replicators download from HuggingFace |
    66	| License | Apache 2.0 (per HF model card) |
    67	| Storage | ~10GB bf16 weights cached at `~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--Qwen--Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct/snapshots/ebb281ec.../` |
    68	
    69	### Decoding
    70	
    71	| Parameter | Value |
    72	|---|---|
    73	| Decoding mode | **Greedy** (`do_sample=False`), bitwise deterministic per (HF SHA + seed + GPU class) |
    74	| Temperature | n/a (greedy) |
    75	| max_new_tokens | per-task (4096 baseline; 50 for Stage 2 patching continuations) |
    76	| Seed | **42** (`configs/exp_v2_base.yaml`) — propagated via `_seed_global_rng()` per (cond, seed) |
    77	| Numerical determinism | bitwise across **A100 80GB / V100 / GB10 within tolerance** (≤1e-6 hidden-state delta per `numerical_determinism_check.py` audit F6). Math SDPA backend forced for cross-architecture portability per B-81h fix. |
    78	
    79	### Capability profile
    80	
    81	- Same VWA agent role as B0 (DOM / SoM / Vision / phantom_som / phantom_dom modes)
    82	- Smaller model → expected weaker SR than B0 (capability contrast is **part of the scientific design**, not a limitation)
    83	- Mechanistic Stage 2 analysis (activation patching) requires open-weights → **only B1 supports paper §5 mechanism claims**
    84	- Layers: 36 transformer blocks (L0 = embedding output, L35 = final post-block); 24 attention heads; hidden dim 2048
    85	
    86	### Limitations
    87	
    88	- **Smaller model**: SR is lower than B0 on most tasks; visual-hijack / click-loop patterns are dominant failure mode (per `section1_intro.md`: B1 70.4% visual-hijack vs B0 53.3% early-finish on disagreement slice)
    89	- **No CoT prefix supplied** (paper-grade convention): agent reasons in `thought` field per VWA prompt template, no scratch-pad CoT trick
    90	- **GPU dependency**: bf16 inference requires sm_70+ (V100 OK, T4 OK with reduced batch); CPU inference too slow for paper-scale runs
    91	- **Cross-machine numerical determinism caveat**: minor (<1e-6) hidden-state drift across V100 vs A100 due to cuDNN kernel selection — bounded under tolerance but worth noting (audit F6)
    92	
    93	---
    94	
    95	## Summary Comparison
    96	
    97	| Dimension | B0 (API) | B1 (local) |
    98	|---|---|---|
    99	| Open weights | ❌ | ✓ |
   100	| Reproducibility | Verifiable from traces | **Byte-identical** |
   101	| Mechanism analysis | Not possible (closed) | Stage 2 patching available |
   102	| SR (typical) | Higher | Lower |
   103	| Cost per episode | $0.01-0.10 | ~free (local compute) |
   104	| Latency | Network-bound (~5-20s) | GPU-bound (~2-10s on A100) |
   105	| Determinism | Best-effort (server-side) | Bitwise (greedy + seed) |
   106	| In-scope for paper §5 mechanism | ❌ Future work (Zoom 4) | ✓ Primary |
   107	
   108	The **B0 vs B1 asymmetry is part of the scientific design**: B0 supplies the
   109	high-capability behavioral characterization, B1 supplies the open-weight
   110	mechanism evidence. Cross-validating mechanism findings on B0 is future
   111	work pending open-weight 235B class models or proxy access to B0 internals.
   112	
   113	## References
   114	
   115	- Mitchell et al. 2019 "Model Cards for Model Reporting" (NEEDS_BIB_ENTRY)
   116	- `pre_run/locked_versions.md` for the exact pinned revision SHAs
   117	- `preregistration.md §7` for reproducibility scope per model
   118	- `negative_results_registry.md` entry #9 for SteerMoE / B0 self-probe retract

## docs/checkpoints/pre_run/evaluator_change_protocol.md
     1	# Evaluator Change Protocol
     2	
     3	**Purpose**: Codify how to handle changes to scoring code (`compute_adjusted_success`,
     4	VWA evaluator wrappers, FP rules). Without an explicit policy, post-lock evaluator
     5	edits become indistinguishable from p-hacking. With this policy, every change is
     6	classified into a tier with a corresponding workflow.
     7	
     8	**Tied to**: `preregistration.md` (commits to FP filter primary = na_fp + eval_fp,
     9	§95 reform); `osf_lock_manifest.md` (8-step DOI lock); `reeval_audit_protocol.md`
    10	(per-episode audit trail).
    11	
    12	**Status**: 🟢 Active (effective from 笔记 §115, 2026-05-07).
    13	
    14	---
    15	
    16	## §1 4-tier classification
    17	
    18	Every change to scoring code (or rules-as-code) falls into exactly one tier.
    19	Pre-lock and post-lock workflows differ; **post-lock = after OSF DOI mint**.
    20	
    21	| Tier | Definition | Examples (real or hypothetical) |
    22	|---|---|---|
    23	| **T0 — Bug fix** | Evaluator logic incorrect vs. its declared spec; spec itself unchanged | §105 Magento radio swatch detection (program_html missed swatch element); evaluator string normalization fix; race-condition retry that was meant to be there |
    24	| **T1 — FP rule expansion** | Adds a new FP category that subsumes more cases as false positive | Hypothetical: discover "url-fragment-only-match" pattern systematically inflating SR — propose new `url_fragment_fp` category |
    25	| **T2 — FP rule simplification / merge** | Removes or merges existing FP categories | §95 deprecating `visual_fp` (no lit precedent + boundary-undecidable + over-filter); §95 simplifying eval_fp from 3-layer to 2-rule |
    26	| **T3 — Definition change** | Redefines what "success" means at the metric level (not the rule level) | Hypothetical: change SR to "weighted SR" with task-difficulty weights; change adjusted_SR formula from `raw ∧ ¬fp` to `raw - α × fp_density` |
    27	
    28	---
    29	
    30	## §2 Pre-lock workflow (advisor email reply NOT yet received)
    31	
    32	Before OSF DOI lock the project still has full flexibility. Discipline:
    33	
    34	| Tier | Action |
    35	|---|---|
    36	| T0 | Fix code → `make rederive RUN=...` on affected runs → 笔记 chronicle entry tagged `[bug]` → commit message prefix `fix(eval):` |
    37	| T1 | Add new FP category in code → run sensitivity check on archived data → discuss with advisor in next sync → preregistration.md amend (single-version, since not yet locked) → 笔记 chronicle `[design]` |
    38	| T2 | Same as T1 (simplification is symmetric to expansion in pre-lock phase) |
    39	| T3 | Treat as "design change" → paper_planning §3 + §19 decision log entry → advisor sync agenda item → preregistration.md substantial rewrite |
    40	
    41	**Common requirement (all tiers)**: every change MUST appear in 笔记 with date, commit SHA, and rationale paragraph. The diff between two consecutive `evaluator_code_sha` values must be 100% explainable from chronicle entries.
    42	
    43	---
    44	
    45	## §3 Post-lock workflow (OSF DOI minted)
    46	
    47	After lock, the witness chain (git tag + email + OSF DOI) freezes the spec.
    48	Rule of thumb: **scoring code may not change in ways that change cell-level
    49	adjusted_SR for any cell in the locked manifest**, except:
    50	
    51	| Tier | Action |
    52	|---|---|
    53	| **T0** | Permitted, BUT: (a) commit message prefix `fix(eval-postlock):`; (b) paper §3 must disclose the bug + which cells affected + magnitude (raw_SR Δ + adjusted_SR Δ); (c) 笔记 entry tagged `[bug][post-lock]`; (d) `make rederive` on all affected cells; (e) re-run `preregistration_decision_test.py` and report BOTH pre-fix and post-fix decision in paper §5 (e.g., "H1: 12/16 pre-fix, 13/16 post-fix; both PASS") |
    54	| **T1** | **Forbidden in same paper.** Either (a) drop the new FP category from this paper and report it as future work, or (b) mint OSF v2 DOI for "preregistration_v2" with the new FP category, cite both v1 and v2 in paper §3, and report decision under both rule sets |
    55	| **T2** | **Forbidden in same paper.** Same as T1 — OSF v2 with new simplified rules, both reported |
    56	| **T3** | **Forbidden in same paper.** Definition change is a new paper. Cite the locked v1 paper, treat T3 as future work / v2 study |
    57	
    58	The commit-message prefix discipline (`fix(eval-postlock):` vs `feat(eval-v2):` vs `paper(metric-redefine):`) lets `git log --grep="eval"` reconstruct the change history at audit time.
    59	
    60	---
    61	
    62	## §4 The "evaluator_code_sha" mechanic
    63	
    64	Every `env_snapshot.json` (auto-dumped at run start since 笔记 §114) carries:
    65	- `evaluator_code` field with `combined_sha256` (SHA256 over concatenated content of files in `EVALUATOR_SOURCE_FILES`)
    66	- `per_file_sha256` (so we can identify which file changed when SHAs diverge)
    67	
    68	Lock-time procedure:
    69	1. `python3 scripts/provenance/snapshot_env.py results/provenance/env_<host>_lock.json` (post-advisor-email)
    70	2. Record `evaluator_code.combined_sha256` in `osf_lock_manifest.md` §2.1
    71	3. After lock, `git diff <commit-of-lock>:p79/experiment/analysis.py HEAD:p79/experiment/analysis.py` should be **empty** unless a T0 fix was made (with proper disclosure).
    72	
    73	Reviewer-defensible claim: "Our scoring code at OSF DOI lock had SHA `abc123...`. Three T0 fixes made post-lock are documented in paper §3.4 with magnitudes."
    74	
    75	---
    76	
    77	## §5 The fp_rule_version string
    78	
    79	Embedded in every `rederive_metadata` entry (per-episode, see Protocol B):
    80	- `§95_v2.0_na_eval` = current (post-§95 reform: na_fp + eval_fp; visual_fp deprecated)
    81	- `§95_v2.0_na_eval_pre_§105` = pre Magento swatch fix (any rederives done with this version had T0 bug present)
    82	- Future hypothetical: `v2.1_na_eval_url_frag` (T1 expansion adding url-fragment FP — only post-lock if OSF v2)
    83	
    84	Bumping `fp_rule_version` in code is itself a Tier classification:
    85	- Patch bump (v2.0 → v2.0.1) = T0 bug fix
    86	- Minor bump (v2.0 → v2.1) = T1 expansion
    87	- Major bump (v2.0 → v3.0) = T2 simplification or T3 redefinition
    88	
    89	---
    90	
    91	## §6 Decision flow
    92	
    93	```
    94	Found a scoring discrepancy → classify it:
    95	├─ Spec & code agree, but real-world behavior unexpected? → T0 bug
    96	│  └─ Pre-lock: rederive + chronicle
    97	│  └─ Post-lock: rederive + chronicle + paper §3 disclose + double-decision report
    98	│
    99	├─ Need a NEW FP category to capture more FPs? → T1 expansion
   100	│  └─ Pre-lock: amend preregistration + advisor confirm
   101	│  └─ Post-lock: OSF v2 DOI, cite both versions
   102	│
   103	├─ Existing FP category broken / inflated? → T2 simplification
   104	│  └─ Pre-lock: amend preregistration + advisor confirm + sensitivity check
   105	│  └─ Post-lock: OSF v2 DOI, cite both versions
   106	│
   107	└─ Want to redefine SR / adjusted_SR formula? → T3 redefinition
   108	   └─ Pre-lock: paper_planning major reframe + advisor sync agenda item
   109	   └─ Post-lock: future work / v2 paper
   110	```
   111	
   112	---
   113	
   114	## §7 Historical retroactive classifications
   115	
   116	Apply this protocol retroactively to past changes for paper §3 audit trail:
   117	
   118	| Change | Date | Tier | Notes |
   119	|---|---|---|---|
   120	| Initial 3-layer FP framework (§78a / §83 / §88) | 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-15 | T1 expansion (pre-lock, no advisor commitment yet) | Original na_fp + eval_fp + visual_fp design |
   121	| §95 reform — drop visual_fp + simplify eval_fp | 2026-04-24 | T2 simplification (pre-lock) | Lit-grounded; preregistration.md updated 2026-05-07 (笔记 §115) |
   122	| §105 Magento radio swatch detection fix | 2026-04-29 | T0 bug fix (pre-lock) | program_html eval was missing swatch elements |
   123	| Phase A 4-cluster fix (commit `3c15cd7`) | 2026-04-30 | T0 bug fix (pre-lock) | runner dispatch / cycle / RNG; not strictly evaluator but score-affecting |
   124	| §114 evaluator_code_sha tracking introduced | 2026-05-07 | (Infra, not eval change) | Enabling this protocol |
   125	
   126	---
   127	
   128	## §8 References
   129	
   130	- 笔记 §78a (na_fp introduction)
   131	- 笔记 §95 (FP reform — visual_fp deprecation rationale + lit anchors)
   132	- 笔记 §105 (Magento radio swatch T0 bug)
   133	- 笔记 §114 (provenance hardening)
   134	- 笔记 §115 (this protocol introduction)
   135	- `p79/experiment/analysis.py:52` (`compute_adjusted_success` canonical impl)

## docs/checkpoints/pre_run/reeval_audit_protocol.md
     1	# Re-evaluation Audit Protocol
     2	
     3	**Purpose**: Codify the audit trail every `make rederive` invocation must leave
     4	behind, so a reviewer asking "this episode's adjusted_SR was re-derived how many
     5	times, by which evaluator code SHA, when, and why?" has a deterministic answer
     6	from `summary.json` alone.
     7	
     8	**Tied to**: `evaluator_change_protocol.md` (Protocol A — Tier classification);
     9	`osf_lock_manifest.md` (lock-time SHA capture); `preregistration.md` (FP filter
    10	primary spec).
    11	
    12	**Status**: 🟢 Active (effective from 笔记 §115, 2026-05-07).
    13	
    14	---
    15	
    16	## §1 What gets audited
    17	
    18	Every successful re-derive of an episode summary writes one entry to a
    19	**list-valued** field `rederive_metadata` in `summary.json`. The list grows
    20	monotonically — old entries are never removed, so the full re-derive history
    21	is preserved.
    22	
    23	```json
    24	{
    25	  "task_id": 0,
    26	  "site": "classifieds",
    27	  "raw_success": true,
    28	  "adjusted_success": false,
    29	  "fp_reason": "eval_fp",
    30	  "rederive_metadata": [
    31	    {
    32	      "rederived_at": "2026-04-25T10:23:01Z",
    33	      "evaluator_code_sha": "<sha256 of analysis.py + environment.py + metrics.py>",
    34	      "fp_rule_version": "§95_v2.0_na_eval",
    35	      "rewrite_set": ["adjusted_success", "fp_reason", "page_unchanged_rate"],
    36	      "trigger": "rederive_episode_summary.py"
    37	    },
    38	    {
    39	      "rederived_at": "2026-04-29T19:12:44Z",
    40	      "evaluator_code_sha": "<different SHA — Magento swatch fix between>",
    41	      "fp_rule_version": "§95_v2.0_na_eval",
    42	      "rewrite_set": ["adjusted_success", "fp_reason", "has_effective_action"],
    43	      "trigger": "rederive_episode_summary.py"
    44	    }
    45	  ]
    46	}
    47	```
    48	
    49	Reviewer audit query:
    50	```bash
    51	jq '.rederive_metadata[] | "\(.rederived_at) [\(.evaluator_code_sha[0:8])] \(.trigger) \(.rewrite_set | join(\",\"))"' \
    52	  results/visualwebarena/phase1/<run>/<cond>/episodes/*_summary_v2.json
    53	```
    54	
    55	---
    56	
    57	## §2 Mandatory fields per entry
    58	
    59	| Field | Type | Source | Why |
    60	|---|---|---|---|
    61	| `rederived_at` | ISO-8601 UTC string | `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` at write time | Temporal ordering across re-derives |
    62	| `evaluator_code_sha` | hex SHA-256 | `hashlib.sha256(...)` over EVALUATOR_SOURCE_FILES | Identifies WHICH evaluator code wrote this re-derive |
    63	| `fp_rule_version` | semver-like string | Hard-coded in `rederive_episode_summary.py` | Identifies WHICH FP rule lineage (e.g., `§95_v2.0_na_eval`) |
    64	| `rewrite_set` | sorted list of strings | Caller-passed `rewrite_set` argument | Identifies WHICH fields the re-derive touched (e.g., not all re-derives touch `adjusted_success`) |
    65	| `trigger` | string | Caller-passed | Free-form trigger identifier (`rederive_episode_summary.py`, `manual`, `migration_v3`, etc) |
    66	
    67	**Write semantics**: append-only. If `rederive_metadata` already exists as a
    68	dict (legacy single-entry format), promote to a list with the legacy entry as
    69	element 0, then append. Never overwrite or truncate.
    70	
    71	---
    72	
    73	## §3 When re-derive is required
    74	
    75	Re-derive is mandatory whenever any of these conditions hold post-data-collection:
    76	
    77	| Condition | Trigger | Affected scope |
    78	|---|---|---|
    79	| **Scoring code change (T0 bug)** per Protocol A | Bug fix commit | All cells whose data was collected pre-fix |
    80	| **FP rule change (T1/T2)** pre-lock | Rule amendment commit | All cells, all sites |
    81	| **`adjusted_success` field missing** | Schema migration | Cells from before §95 reform |
    82	| **Bug-affected derived field** (e.g., `page_unchanged_rate`, `energy_partial`) | §97 audit findings | Cells from before audit |
    83	
    84	Re-derive is NOT done for:
    85	- Adding new derived fields that don't change SR (e.g., adding `rederive_metadata` itself — bootstrapped lazily on next legitimate re-derive)
    86	- Cosmetic refactors (renaming, type hints)
    87	- Documentation-only commits
    88	
    89	---
    90	
    91	## §4 Re-derive idempotency
    92	
    93	The current `rederive_episode_summary.py` writes to `episodes/.bak_pre_rederive/<orig_name>` once (one-shot, never overwrites existing backup). This Protocol B layer adds a second idempotency invariant:
    94	
    95	**Repeated `make rederive RUN=<R>` invocations with no code change between them**:
    96	- ✅ Episode summary unchanged (fast-path: §95 fast-path skips if `adjusted_success` already present and FP rules unchanged)
    97	- ⚠️ `rederive_metadata` list **does grow by one entry per invocation** (each entry has the same SHA but different `rederived_at`)
    98	
    99	If you do not want spam entries, use `make rederive` only when there's an actual reason. The Protocol A workflow makes this explicit.
   100	
   101	---
   102	
   103	## §5 Backup files
   104	
   105	Original (pre-first-rederive) `summary_v2.json` → backed up to `episodes/.bak_pre_rederive/<filename>` once. Used for:
   106	1. Disaster recovery (revert to known-good pre-rederive state)
   107	2. Diff inspection ("what did rederive change?") via:
   108	   ```bash
   109	   diff <(jq -S . episodes/.bak_pre_rederive/cls_task_0_summary_v2.json) \
   110	        <(jq -S . episodes/cls_task_0_summary_v2.json)
   111	   ```
   112	
   113	Backups are NEVER deleted by `rederive_episode_summary.py`. If the user wants to start fresh, manual `rm -rf .bak_pre_rederive/` is required (and not advised).
   114	
   115	---
   116	
   117	## §6 OSF DOI lock interaction
   118	
   119	At OSF DOI lock (Protocol A §3, `osf_lock_manifest.md` 8-step workflow):
   120	1. All cells in `run_manifest.yaml` with `grade=paper-grade` must have `rederive_metadata` non-empty
   121	2. The most recent `evaluator_code_sha` across all locked cells must match the lock-time `evaluator_code.combined_sha256` from `env_snapshot.json`
   122	3. If any cell has an `evaluator_code_sha` that differs from the lock-time SHA → MUST re-derive that cell pre-lock, OR document the discrepancy in `osf_lock_manifest.md` §2.5 with rationale
   123	
   124	**Lock-time check script** (paper-grade gate, to be added to `queue_16cell_paper_grade.sh` Gate 7):
   125	```bash
   126	python3 scripts/provenance/check_evaluator_consistency.py --manifest run_manifest.yaml \
   127	  --lock-snapshot results/provenance/env_<host>_lock.json
   128	# Exits 0 if all cells' most-recent evaluator_code_sha == lock SHA, 1 otherwise
   129	```
   130	
   131	(This script is **not yet implemented** — flagged in `next_steps.md` §4 audit
   132	follow-ups as R6.)
   133	
   134	---
   135	
   136	## §7 Post-lock re-derive (rare, requires Protocol A T0 disclosure)
   137	
   138	Per Protocol A §3, T0 bug fixes ARE permitted post-lock with proper disclosure.
   139	The re-derive workflow then becomes:
   140	
   141	1. T0 bug fix committed with prefix `fix(eval-postlock):`
   142	2. `make rederive RUN=<each affected run>` runs as usual; new entry in
   143	   `rederive_metadata` shows new SHA
   144	3. `osf_lock_manifest.md` §4 records: "Post-lock T0 fix: `fix(eval-postlock):
   145	   <commit-msg>` on YYYY-MM-DD; affected cells: <list>; magnitude:
   146	   ΔadjSR_max=X.Xpp"
   147	4. Paper §3.4 prose updated to disclose
   148	5. `preregistration_decision_test.py` re-run; both pre-fix and post-fix decision
   149	   reported in paper §5
   150	
   151	**The audit trail in `rederive_metadata` is what makes this defensible** — the
   152	diverging SHA in the post-lock entry is the immutable evidence.
   153	
   154	---
   155	
   156	## §8 References
   157	
   158	- 笔记 §97 (rederive_episode_summary.py introduction + `.bak_pre_rederive`)
   159	- 笔记 §115 (this protocol introduction)
   160	- `scripts/maintenance/rederive_episode_summary.py` (the canonical re-derive)
   161	- `scripts/provenance/snapshot_env.py` (`evaluator_code` field in env snapshot)
   162	- `docs/checkpoints/pre_run/evaluator_change_protocol.md` (Protocol A — Tier classification)
   163	- `docs/checkpoints/pre_run/osf_lock_manifest.md` (lock-time SHA capture)
   164	- `docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md` (FP filter primary commitment)
   165	- Pre-launch gate: `scripts/queues/queue_16cell_paper_grade.sh` Gate 7 (TODO)

## docs/checkpoints/pre_run/negative_results_registry.md
     1	# Negative Results Registry
     2	
     3	> Open-science discipline (Nosek et al. 2015; Lipton & Steinhardt 2018):
     4	> failed pilots, retracted framings, and abandoned hypotheses are documented
     5	> here so the final paper narrative is **constrained by what we tried**, not
     6	> just by what worked. Reviewers who diff archived branches against published
     7	> claims should find every framing pivot recorded.
     8	>
     9	> This addresses audit constraints **H2** (negative-result registry) and
    10	> **D8/H5** ("controlled characterization" framing — see paper_planning §21-§22).

    22	| **2** | 2026-05-01 | **Phantom-SoM is hidden 4th routing arm** | **Phantom routing space (3 arms: P-text / P-prompt / P-SoM) sharing 4-fold drop-in property** | B0 reddit 6-mode oracle vs 3-mode +7.14pp [3.81, 10.48] sig + 3 arms drop-one all sig → "1 arm" framing literally inaccurate; "1 routing dimension" stronger venue claim | Paper hook §1 reframe; provisional pending data confirm; advisor sync Q3 |
    23	| **3** | 2026-05-01 | **8-corner 2x2x2 cube factorial design** as paper §2 axis | **M1/M2 mechanism activation 2x2** (LLM internal state level, not prompt structure level) | Prompt-text coupling ≠ mechanism activation coupling; 8-corner conflated levels | Memory `project_paper_hook.md` retract list; paper §2 rewrite |
    24	| **4** | 2026-05-01 | **6-corner asymmetric grid** (a/b × c/¬c × 1/2) | M1/M2 2x2 (4-corner) | Same level-confusion as #3 | Same retract list |

    29	| **9** | 2026-05-01 | **SteerMoE-style expert routing self-probe** for B0 | Zoom 4 future work direction (paper §8), no self-probe | B0 is proxy API → model internals invisible; local 235B deploy budget exceeds RunPod $200 allocation | Paper §8 future work |

## docs/checkpoints/pre_run/osf_lock_manifest.md
     1	# OSF DOI Lock Manifest — Paper §3 / Appendix D
     2	
     3	**Purpose**: Codify the artefacts whose SHA-256 / git ref get frozen at the
     4	moment of OSF preregistration DOI minting. Once advisor's email reply arrives
     5	(post 5/5 sync) confirming K_h1 / K_h3 / TOST δ thresholds, this checklist
     6	drives the 8-step DOI workflow (笔记 §110 + ADVISOR_SYNC §F).
     7	
     8	**Status**: 🟡 Draft — fields populate at lock moment.
     9	**Lock blocker**: ⏳ advisor email reply (Q1-Q11 in `advisor_sync_5_5_followup.md`)
    10	
    11	---
    12	
    13	## §1 Pre-lock checklist (everything must be done before OSF DOI mint)
    14	
    15	- [ ] Advisor email reply received (K_h1=0.75, K_h3=0.67, TOST δ=1.0pp confirmed
    16	      OR alternative thresholds noted)
    17	- [ ] `preregistration.md` final text edit committed + pushed
    18	- [ ] `run_manifest.yaml` archived rows verified (16-cell scope, all
    19	      `grade=archived` for pre-rerun cells, `grade=paper-grade` post-rerun cells)
    20	- [ ] All paper draft sections section1-8 + paper.bib (57 entries) snapshot to
    21	      `docs/checkpoints/paper_drafts_locked/` directory (immutable copy)
    22	- [ ] `env_snapshot.json` of latest run on each machine (DGX, A100, Myriad if
    23	      used) committed under `results/provenance/env_lock_<hostname>.json`
    24	- [ ] `vwa_snapshot_<host>.json` for any VWA-using cells committed
    25	- [ ] No untracked / uncommitted files in repo (clean `git status`)
    26	- [ ] Repo pushed to GitHub master (DOI cites GitHub commit URL)

    73	## §3 Eight-step DOI workflow (post advisor email reply)
    74	
    75	1. **Receive advisor reply** → save email PDF + extract Gmail message-id
    76	2. **Update `preregistration.md`** with confirmed thresholds + decision log entry
    77	3. **Run `python3 scripts/provenance/snapshot_env.py`** on DGX + A100 (+ Myriad
    78	   if used), commit results under `results/provenance/env_lock_<host>.json`
    79	4. **Run `bash scripts/provenance/snapshot_vwa.sh`** on each VWA-bearing host,
    80	   commit results
    81	5. **Snapshot paper drafts** → `cp -r paper_drafts paper_drafts_locked` + commit
    82	6. **Tag git** → `git tag -a preregistration-locked -m "OSF DOI mint $(date)"`
    83	   + `git push origin preregistration-locked`
    84	7. **Mint OSF DOI** at https://osf.io/registries/ — link OSF page to the tagged
    85	   commit URL on GitHub (https://github.com/<user>/<repo>/tree/preregistration-locked)
    86	8. **Backfill this manifest** — populate all `<TBD>` cells with actual SHAs +
    87	   timestamps + DOI; commit as final lock proof
    88	
    89	After Step 8, **no edits permitted** to any file referenced in §2 except via
    90	new commits explicitly noted as "post-lock amendment" in `paper_planning.md` §19
    91	decision log + paper §3 disclosure paragraph.

    96	
    97	If advisor / reviewer pushes for threshold change post-lock:
    98	- **NEW** preregistration document added (`preregistration_v2.md`) — DOI'd
    99	  separately
   100	- v1 + v2 both cited in paper §3
   101	- Each pre-spec block in paper §5 footnoted with "matches v1 OSF lock at
   102	  YYYY-MM-DD" or "amended in v2 OSF lock"
   103	
   104	This avoids the "moving goalpost" critique while enabling honest threshold
   105	revision when data warrants.
