   129	    def _make_dom_prompt(self) -> str:
   130	        return """You are a precise web navigation agent.
   131	Output ONLY valid JSON. No markdown blocks, no explanations.
   132	
   133	You receive the full Accessibility Tree of the current page.
   134	Use element IDs from the Accessibility Tree to interact with elements.
   135	
   136	Core Rules:
   137	1) Do NOT answer or finish immediately. You MUST navigate to find the item.
   138	2) You are logged in as a user. For tasks involving your own content (e.g., "my listing", "my post", "my message"),
   139	   navigate to account/profile sections instead of searching publicly.
   140	3) If the target category is not visible, look for a parent category or use the search bar.
   141	4) NEVER give up early. If you don't see the item, SEARCH for it using the search bar.
   142	5) Only use "finish" when you have successfully completed the task or after EXHAUSTIVE search.
   143	6) For single-item tasks (find and navigate to ONE specific item/page), you MUST open that item's detail page before "finish".
   144	   For collection tasks (return links/info for MULTIPLE items), you MAY "finish" from a list/search page
   145	   after recording the required items in your answer.
   146	7) If you are on the homepage, DO NOT go back. Start by searching or clicking a category.
   147	8) If you are stuck, use scroll or try a different category/search.
   148	
   149	Response Format (JSON):
   150	{
   151	  "thought": "Brief reasoning about what to do next.",
   152	  "confidence": 0.0 to 1.0,
   153	  "action_type": "click" | "type" | "select_option" | "scroll" | "wait" | "back" | "forward" | "finish" | "tab_focus",
   154	  ... (other action parameters) ...
   155	}
   156	"confidence": your self-assessed probability (0.0–1.0) that this action makes meaningful progress toward the task goal.
   157	
   158	Action Schema:
   159	1. Click: {"action_type": "click", "element_id": N}
   160	   - N is the numeric ID from the Accessibility Tree (e.g., [175] link 'Comments' -> element_id: 175).
   161	   - ALWAYS prefer element_id. Only use coordinate as last resort.
   162	2. Type: {"action_type": "type", "text": "string", "element_id": N}
   163	   - This action automatically clicks the target to focus it, then types the text.
   164	   - ALWAYS use "type" (not "click") when you want to enter text into an input field.
   165	   - "click" is for buttons, links, and navigation only — it cannot enter text.
   166	   - ALWAYS specify element_id to target the correct input field.
   167	   - To submit, append "\\n" to the text.
   168	2.5. Select Option: {"action_type": "select_option", "element_id": N, "option_label": "Option Name"}
   169	   - Use ONLY for <select> dropdown elements (shown as "combobox" in the Accessibility Tree).
   170	   - Clicking a combobox does NOT open the dropdown. Use select_option instead.
   171	   - option_label must match the visible option text exactly (e.g., "Electronics", "Jewelry & Watches").
   172	3. Scroll: {"action_type": "scroll", "delta": [dx, dy], "coordinate_type": "normalized"}
   173	   - dy>0 scrolls DOWN, dy<0 scrolls UP. Use scroll up when the target is above the current view.
   174	4. Wait: {"action_type": "wait"}
   175	5. Back: {"action_type": "back"} — WARNING: Do NOT use on the first/homepage.
   176	6. Forward: {"action_type": "forward"}
   177	7. Finish: {"action_type": "finish", "answer": "optional string"}
   178	8. Tab focus: {"action_type": "tab_focus", "page_number": int}
   179	
   180	Tab Rule:
   181	- Multi-site tasks may open multiple tabs (different websites).
   182	- If the target website is in another tab, switch with {"action_type":"tab_focus","page_number":N} BEFORE clicking.
   183	- Element IDs are page-local to the current tab. Do NOT reuse IDs from another tab/site.
   184	- Do NOT try to find a cross-site navigation link on the current page when the site is already in another tab.
   185	
   186	CRITICAL:
   187	- You MUST include a "thought" field.
   188	- ALWAYS use element_id for click and type. Do NOT guess coordinates.
   189	- Do NOT output literal newlines inside JSON strings. Use \\n.
   190	- Avoid repeating the same action. Change strategy if stuck.
   191	"""
   192	
   193	    def _make_som_prompt(self) -> str:
   194	        return """You are a precise web navigation agent.
   195	Output ONLY valid JSON. No markdown blocks, no explanations.
   196	
   197	You receive:
   198	  1. A [SOM_MARKS] list: flat index of interactive elements, each with [id=N] and a short description.
   199	  2. A screenshot — normally with bounding boxes labeled by ID, matching the [SOM_MARKS] list.
   200	
   201	Note: If [SOM_MARKS] is empty (no elements detected), no bounding boxes will appear in the screenshot.
   202	In that case, fall back to coordinate-based interaction using what you can see in the screenshot.
   203	
   204	Use the element IDs from [SOM_MARKS] to interact. Use the screenshot to understand spatial layout and locate elements not in the list.
   205	
   206	Core Rules:
   207	1) Do NOT answer or finish immediately. You MUST navigate to find the item.
   208	2) You are logged in as a user. For tasks involving your own content (e.g., "my listing", "my post", "my message"),
   209	   navigate to account/profile sections instead of searching publicly.
   210	3) Prefer element_id for clicks and typing. Use coordinate only when the target is visible in the image but has no ID in [SOM_MARKS].
   211	4) NEVER give up early. If you don't see the item, SEARCH for it using the search bar.
   212	5) Only use "finish" when you have successfully completed the task or after EXHAUSTIVE search.
   213	6) For single-item tasks (find and navigate to ONE specific item/page), you MUST open that item's detail page before "finish".
   214	   For collection tasks (return links/info for MULTIPLE items), you MAY "finish" from a list/search page
   215	   after recording the required items in your answer.
   216	7) If you are on the homepage, DO NOT go back. Start by searching or clicking a category.
   217	8) If you are stuck, scroll or try a different approach.
   218	
   219	Response Format (JSON):
   220	{
   221	  "thought": "Brief reasoning about what to do next.",
   222	  "confidence": 0.0 to 1.0,
   223	  "action_type": "click" | "type" | "select_option" | "scroll" | "wait" | "back" | "forward" | "finish" | "tab_focus",
   224	  ... (other action parameters) ...
   225	}
   226	"confidence": your self-assessed probability (0.0–1.0) that this action makes meaningful progress toward the task goal.
   227	
   228	Action Schema:
   229	1. Click by element_id (preferred): {"action_type": "click", "element_id": N}
   230	   - N is from [SOM_MARKS], e.g. [id=175] link 'Comments' -> element_id: 175.
   231	2. Click by coordinate (fallback): {"action_type": "click", "coordinate": [x, y], "coordinate_type": "normalized"}
   232	   - x, y are floats 0.0–1.0. Use only when no element_id is available.
   233	3. Type: {"action_type": "type", "text": "string", "element_id": N}
   234	   - This action automatically clicks the target to focus it, then types the text.
   235	   - ALWAYS use "type" (not "click") when you want to enter text into an input field.
   236	   - "click" is for buttons, links, and navigation only — it cannot enter text.
   237	   - Prefer element_id. To submit, append "\\n" to the text.
   238	3.5. Select Option: {"action_type": "select_option", "element_id": N, "option_label": "Option Name"}
   239	   - Use ONLY for <select> dropdown elements (shown as "combobox" in the SOM_MARKS list).
   240	   - Clicking a combobox does NOT open the dropdown. Use select_option instead.
   241	   - option_label must match the visible option text exactly (e.g., "Electronics", "Jewelry & Watches").
   242	4. Scroll: {"action_type": "scroll", "delta": [dx, dy], "coordinate_type": "normalized"}
   243	   - dy>0 scrolls DOWN, dy<0 scrolls UP. Use scroll up when the target is above the current view.
   244	5. Wait: {"action_type": "wait"}
   245	6. Back: {"action_type": "back"} — WARNING: Do NOT use on the first/homepage.
   246	7. Forward: {"action_type": "forward"}
   247	8. Finish: {"action_type": "finish", "answer": "optional string"}
   248	9. Tab focus: {"action_type": "tab_focus", "page_number": int}
   249	
   250	Tab Rule:
   251	- Multi-site tasks may open multiple tabs (different websites).
   252	- If the target website is in another tab, switch with {"action_type":"tab_focus","page_number":N} BEFORE clicking.
   253	- Element IDs are page-local to the current tab. Do NOT reuse IDs from another tab/site.
   254	- Do NOT try to find a cross-site navigation link on the current page when the site is already in another tab.
   255	
   256	CRITICAL:
   257	- You MUST include a "thought" field.
   258	- Prefer element_id over coordinate when the element appears in [SOM_MARKS].
   259	- Do NOT output literal newlines inside JSON strings. Use \\n.
   260	- Avoid repeating the same action. Change strategy if stuck.

   100	class ProxyApiAgent:
   101	    """Agent that talks to a custom proxy endpoint (Anthropic Messages API style).
   102	
   103	    Request:  POST endpoint  { model, messages, max_tokens, temperature, system }
   104	    Response: { content: [{type:"text", text:"..."}], model, usage, metadata }
   105	    Auth:     X-Api-Key header
   106	    """
   107	
   108	    def __init__(self, config: Dict[str, Any]):
   109	        self.config = config
   110	        model_cfg = config.get("model", {})
   111	        self.model_name = model_cfg.get("api_name", "qwen.qwen3-vl-235b-a22b")
   112	
   113	        # API format: "anthropic" (proxy default) or "openai" (DashScope, etc.)
   114	        self._api_format = model_cfg.get("api_format", "anthropic")
   115	        # Image format in messages: "openai" (image_url) or "anthropic_native" (source base64).
   116	        # Auto-detect from model name if not set explicitly.
   117	        self._image_format = model_cfg.get("image_format", "auto")
   118	        if self._image_format == "auto":
   119	            if "anthropic" in self.model_name.lower() or "claude" in self.model_name.lower():
   120	                self._image_format = "anthropic_native"
   121	            else:
   122	                self._image_format = "openai"
   123	
   124	        self.endpoint = model_cfg.get("base_url") or os.getenv("PROXY_API_ENDPOINT", "")
   125	        if not self.endpoint:
   126	            raise RuntimeError(
   127	                "Proxy API endpoint not set. "
   128	                "Set model.base_url in config or PROXY_API_ENDPOINT env var."
   129	            )
   130	        # OpenAI format: ensure endpoint ends with /chat/completions
   131	        if self._api_format == "openai":
   132	            ep = self.endpoint.rstrip("/")
   133	            if not ep.endswith("/chat/completions"):
   134	                self.endpoint = ep + "/chat/completions"
   135	            else:
   136	                self.endpoint = ep
   137	
   138	        api_key_env = model_cfg.get("api_key_env", "PROXY_API_KEY")
   139	        self.api_key = os.getenv(api_key_env) or ""
   140	        if not self.api_key:
   141	            raise RuntimeError(f"{api_key_env} environment variable is not set")
   142	
   143	        self.timeout = model_cfg.get("timeout", _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
   144	        self._use_tool_calling = model_cfg.get("use_tool_calling", False)
   145	
   146	        # GLM fallback for parse-error recovery (Solution B).
   147	        # Reads .auth/glm (3-line file: endpoint, model, api_key).
   148	        # Cost is NOT counted in experiment metrics — purely scaffold overhead.
   149	        self._glm_config: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None
   150	        glm_cfg_path = model_cfg.get("glm_config", ".auth/glm")
   151	        if model_cfg.get("use_glm_fallback", False):
   152	            self._glm_config = self._load_glm_config(glm_cfg_path)
   153	
   154	        self._system_prompts = self._get_system_prompts()
   155	
   156	        # When tool calling is enabled, replace the "output JSON" instruction
   157	        # with a tool-use instruction.  This is a format-only change — the
   158	        # rules, action schema, and all task-relevant guidance are unchanged.
   159	        if self._use_tool_calling:
   160	            _old = "Output ONLY valid JSON. No markdown blocks, no explanations."
   161	            _new = "Use the web_action tool for every action. Put reasoning in the thought parameter."
   162	            for mode in self._system_prompts:
   163	                self._system_prompts[mode] = self._system_prompts[mode].replace(_old, _new)
   164	
   165	    # ---- GLM fallback (Solution B) ----
   166	
   167	    @staticmethod
   168	    def _load_glm_config(cfg_path: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, str]]:
   169	        """Load GLM config from a 3-line file: endpoint, model, api_key."""
   170	        p = Path(cfg_path)
   171	        if not p.exists():
   172	            logger.warning("GLM config %s not found; GLM fallback disabled.", cfg_path)
   173	            return None
   174	        lines = [
   175	            ln.strip()
   176	            for ln in p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
   177	            if ln.strip() and not ln.strip().startswith("#")
   178	        ]
   179	        if len(lines) < 3:
   180	            logger.warning("GLM config %s needs 3 lines (endpoint/model/key); got %d. Disabled.", cfg_path, len(lines))
   181	            return None
   182	        cfg = {"endpoint": lines[0], "model": lines[1], "api_key": lines[2]}
   183	        logger.info("GLM fallback enabled: model=%s", cfg["model"])
   184	        return cfg
   185	
   186	    def _call_glm_extract(self, raw_output: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
   187	        """Ask GLM to extract a JSON action from raw model output.
   188	
   189	        Returns validated action dict on success, None on failure.
   190	        This is a scaffold-level format repair — cost is NOT experiment cost.
   191	        """
   192	        if not self._glm_config:
   193	            return None
   194	
   195	        # Truncate to avoid sending huge payloads for a simple extraction task.
   196	        truncated = raw_output[:4000]
   197	        extract_prompt = (
   198	            "Extract or infer the intended web navigation action from the following agent output.\n"
   199	            "The output may be valid JSON, malformed JSON, or natural language describing the intended action.\n\n"
   200	            "Rules:\n"
   201	            '- Output a single JSON object with "action_type" (one of: click, type, scroll, wait, back, '
   202	            "forward, finish, select_option, tab_focus).\n"
   203	            "- Include relevant fields: element_id, coordinate, text, scroll_direction (up/down), "
   204	            "option_label, answer, thought.\n"
   205	            "- If the output contains JSON (possibly malformed), extract and fix it.\n"
   206	            "- If the output is natural language, infer the action from the described intent.\n"
   207	            '- For finish/stop actions, extract the answer from context (do NOT leave answer as "").\n'
   208	            "- Output ONLY the JSON object. No explanation, no markdown.\n\n"
   209	            "Examples:\n"
   210	            'Input: "I need to click on the submit button which is element 42"\n'
   211	            'Output: {"action_type": "click", "element_id": 42, "thought": "click submit button"}\n\n'
   212	            'Input: "Let me scroll down to see more results on this page"\n'
   213	            'Output: {"action_type": "scroll", "scroll_direction": "down", "thought": "scroll to see more results"}\n\n'
   214	            'Input: "The answer to the question is $25.99, I should finish now"\n'
   215	            'Output: {"action_type": "finish", "answer": "$25.99", "thought": "found the answer"}\n\n'
   216	            f"Agent output:\n{truncated}"
   217	        )
   218	
   219	        messages = [
   220	            {"role": "system", "content": "You extract or infer structured JSON actions from agent output. Output ONLY valid JSON."},
   221	            {"role": "user", "content": extract_prompt},
   222	        ]
   223	        payload = json.dumps({
   224	            "model": self._glm_config["model"],
   225	            "messages": messages,
   226	            "temperature": 0.0,
   227	            # GLM-5.1 is a thinking model: reasoning_content consumes most of the
   228	            # token budget.  512 causes content truncation for complex outputs.
   229	            "max_tokens": 2048,
   230	        }).encode("utf-8")
   231	
   232	        ep = self._glm_config["endpoint"].rstrip("/")

    37	                for cell in get_cells(baseline=baseline, site=site)
    38	            }
    39	    return out

    41	
    42	BASELINE_ORDER = ["B0", "B1"]
    43	SITE_ORDER = ["reddit", "classifieds"]
    44	SUMMARY_DIRS = _summary_dirs_from_registry()
    45	MODE_ORDER = PAPER_MODES
    46	
    47	
    48	def task_id(path: Path) -> int:
    49	    match = re.search(r"task_(\d+)_summary", path.name)
    50	    if not match:
    51	        raise ValueError(f"Cannot parse task id from {path}")
    52	    return int(match.group(1))
    53	
    54	
    55	def read_json(path: Path) -> Any:
    56	    return json.loads(path.read_text())
    57	
    58	
    59	def pct(num: int, den: int) -> float:
    60	    return 100.0 * num / den if den else 0.0
    61	
    62	
    63	def aggregate_cell(baseline: str, site: str, mode: str, ep_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    64	    rows: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    65	    for path in sorted(ep_dir.glob("*_summary_v2.json")):
    66	        tid = task_id(path)
    67	        if tid in rows:
    68	            print(f"[warn] duplicate task summary ignored for {baseline}/{site}/{mode}: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
    69	            continue
    70	        rows[tid] = read_json(path)
    71	
    72	    n_total = len(rows)
    73	    n_raw_success = 0
    74	    n_adjusted_success = 0
    75	    fp_count = 0
    76	    fp_breakdown: Counter[str] = Counter()
    77	
    78	    # F26 audit fix 2026-05-09: track rows missing `adjusted_success` so
    79	    # SR aggregation never silently substitutes raw success for the
    80	    # locked adjusted SR. Strict mode (env P79_STRICT=1) raises; default
    81	    # warns + counts in fp_breakdown.
    82	    n_missing_adjusted = 0
    83	    strict = os.environ.get("P79_STRICT", "").lower() in ("1", "true", "yes")
    84	
    85	    for row in rows.values():
    86	        raw = bool(row.get("success", False))
    87	        if "adjusted_success" not in row or row.get("adjusted_success") is None:
    88	            n_missing_adjusted += 1
    89	            adjusted = raw  # legacy fallback, but flagged
    90	        else:
    91	            adjusted = bool(row["adjusted_success"])
    92	        n_raw_success += int(raw)
    93	        n_adjusted_success += int(adjusted)
    94	        if raw and not adjusted:
    95	            fp_count += 1
    96	            reason = str(row.get("fp_reason") or "").strip() if "fp_reason" in row else ""
    97	            fp_breakdown[reason or "unspecified"] += 1
    98	
    99	    if n_missing_adjusted > 0:
   100	        msg = (
   101	            f"[{baseline}/{site}/{mode}] {n_missing_adjusted}/{n_total} "
   102	            "rows missing `adjusted_success` field — fell back to raw success. "
   103	            "This violates preregistration §4 FP filter lock. "
   104	            "Set P79_STRICT=1 to fail-closed."
   105	        )
   106	        if strict:
   107	            raise RuntimeError(msg)
   108	        else:
   109	            print(f"WARNING: {msg}")
   110	
   111	    return {
   112	        "baseline": baseline,
   113	        "site": site,
   114	        "mode": mode,
   115	        "n_total": n_total,
   116	        "n_raw_success": n_raw_success,
   117	        "n_adjusted_success": n_adjusted_success,
   118	        "raw_sr_pct": round(pct(n_raw_success, n_total), 6),
   119	        "adjusted_sr_pct": round(pct(n_adjusted_success, n_total), 6),
   120	        "fp_count": fp_count,
   121	        "fp_rate_pct": round(pct(fp_count, n_total), 6),
   122	        "fp_breakdown": dict(sorted(fp_breakdown.items())),
   123	        "source_dir": str(ep_dir.relative_to(ROOT)),
   124	    }
   125	
   126	
   127	def fmt_pct(value: float) -> str:
   128	    return f"{value:.2f}%"
   129	
   130	
   131	def write_markdown(summary_table: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
   132	    lines: list[str] = []
   133	    lines.append("# SR + FP per Mode")
   134	    lines.append("")
   135	    lines.append("Standalone Outcome 0a/0b aggregation from paper-grade per-task `summary_v2.json` files (B0 + B1).")
   136	    lines.append("")
   137	    lines.append("## Main Table")
   138	    lines.append("")
   139	    lines.append("| baseline | site | mode | n | raw SR | adjusted SR | FP count | FP rate | FP breakdown |")
   140	    lines.append("|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|")
   141	    for row in summary_table:
   142	        breakdown = ", ".join(f"{reason}={count}" for reason, count in row["fp_breakdown"].items()) or "none"
   143	        lines.append(
   144	            f"| {row['baseline']} | {row['site']} | {row['mode']} | {row['n_total']} | "
   145	            f"{fmt_pct(row['raw_sr_pct'])} | {fmt_pct(row['adjusted_sr_pct'])} | "
   146	            f"{row['fp_count']} | {fmt_pct(row['fp_rate_pct'])} | {breakdown} |"
   147	        )
   148	
   149	    lines.append("")
   150	    lines.append("## FP rate ranking per (baseline, site)")
   151	    lines.append("")
   152	    for baseline in BASELINE_ORDER:
   153	        for site in SITE_ORDER:
   154	            rows = [row for row in summary_table if row["baseline"] == baseline and row["site"] == site]
   155	            if not rows:
   156	                continue
   157	            rows.sort(key=lambda row: (row["fp_rate_pct"], row["mode"]))
   158	            ranking = " < ".join(f"{row['mode']} {fmt_pct(row['fp_rate_pct'])}" for row in rows)
   159	            lines.append(f"- {baseline} {site}: {ranking}")
   160	
   161	    lines.append("")
   162	    lines.append("## Method")
   163	    lines.append("")
   164	    lines.append(
   165	        "Raw SR counts `success == true`; adjusted SR counts `adjusted_success == true` "
   166	        "with fallback to `success` when the adjusted field is absent. FP count is raw success minus adjusted success. "
   167	        "B1 phantom data is partial: only B1 classifieds Phantom-SoM is available (P-text pending, B1 reddit phantom pending)."
   168	    )
   169	    OUT_MD.write_text("\n".join(lines).rstrip() + "\n")
   170	
   171	
   172	def main() -> None:
   173	    summary_table: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   174	    cells: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
   175	    for baseline in BASELINE_ORDER:
   176	        baseline_dirs = SUMMARY_DIRS.get(baseline, {})
   177	        for site in SITE_ORDER:
   178	            site_dirs = baseline_dirs.get(site, {})
   179	            for mode in MODE_ORDER:
   180	                ep_dir = site_dirs.get(mode)
   181	                if ep_dir is None:
   182	                    continue
   183	                if not ep_dir.exists():
   184	                    # Path resolved (e.g. P-prompt glob) but the run dir does
   185	                    # not exist yet — cell pending, skip silently.
   186	                    continue
   187	                cell = aggregate_cell(baseline, site, mode, ep_dir)
   188	                if cell["n_total"] == 0:
   189	                    continue
   190	                cells[f"{baseline}/{site}/{mode}"] = cell
   191	                summary_table.append(cell)
   192	
   193	    out = {
   194	        "method": "aggregate raw/adjusted SR + FP from per-task summary_v2.json (B0 5-mode + B1 partial)",
   195	        "data_source": "paper-grade B0 5-mode runs + B1 3-mode + B1 cls Phantom-SoM (FRESH 04-29)",
   196	        "cells": cells,
   197	        "summary_table": summary_table,
   198	    }
   199	    OUT_JSON.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   200	    OUT_JSON.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2) + "\n")
   201	    write_markdown(summary_table)
   202	    print(f"[json] {OUT_JSON}")
   203	    print(f"[md] {OUT_MD}")
   204	
   205	
   206	if __name__ == "__main__":
   207	    main()

    32	MODES = ["DOM", "SoM", "Vision", "P-text", "P-prompt", "P-SoM"]

    35	def emit_placeholder(reason: str):

    45	def main():
    46	    if not SRC.exists():
    47	        emit_placeholder(f"missing source {SRC.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    48	        return
    49	    data = json.loads(SRC.read_text())
    50	    rows = data.get("summary_table", [])
    51	    if not rows:
    52	        emit_placeholder("summary_table empty — run `make aggregate-sr-fp` after baseline runs")
    53	        return
    54	
    55	    # Build cell grid: row_keys=(baseline, site), col=mode → adj_sr_pct
    56	    seen_rows = {}
    57	    for r in rows:
    58	        baseline = r.get("baseline", "?")
    59	        site = r.get("site", "?")
    60	        mode = r.get("mode", "?")
    61	        adj = r.get("adjusted_sr_pct", r.get("adj_sr_pct"))
    62	        if adj is None:
    63	            continue
    64	        key = (baseline, site)
    65	        seen_rows.setdefault(key, {})[mode] = r
    66	
    67	    if not seen_rows:

    69	        return
    70	
    71	    row_keys = sorted(seen_rows.keys())
    72	    grid = np.full((len(row_keys), len(MODES)), np.nan)
    73	    annot = [["" for _ in MODES] for _ in row_keys]
    74	    for i, rk in enumerate(row_keys):
    75	        for j, m in enumerate(MODES):
    76	            r = seen_rows[rk].get(m)
    77	            if r is None:

    79	            adj = r.get("adjusted_sr_pct", r.get("adj_sr_pct"))

    83	            fp = r.get("fp_count", 0)

    92	    masked = np.ma.masked_invalid(grid)
    93	    im = ax.imshow(masked, cmap=cmap, aspect="auto", vmin=0,
    94	                   vmax=max(25, np.nanmax(grid) if np.isfinite(grid).any() else 25))
    95	    for i in range(len(row_keys)):
    96	        for j in range(len(MODES)):
    97	            if np.isnan(grid[i, j]):
    98	                ax.text(j, i, "—", ha="center", va="center", color="gray", fontsize=9)
    99	            else:
   100	                color = "white" if grid[i, j] > 12 else "black"
   101	                ax.text(j, i, annot[i][j], ha="center", va="center", color=color, fontsize=7.5)

   103	    ax.set_xticks(range(len(MODES)))
   104	    ax.set_xticklabels(MODES, fontsize=10)
   105	    ax.set_yticks(range(len(row_keys)))
   106	    ax.set_yticklabels([f"{b} · {s}" for b, s in row_keys], fontsize=10)
   107	    ax.set_title("Adjusted success rate (%) per (baseline, site) × mode\npaper §1 0a — main hook",
   108	                 fontsize=12)

   112	             fontsize=6.5, color="gray")
   113	    fig.tight_layout()
   114	    fig.savefig(OUT, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
   115	    plt.close(fig)

     2	"""[Outcome 0b] FP rate per mode — paper §1 hygiene figure.
     3	
     4	Reads docs/analysis/cross_sites/sr_fp_per_mode.json and emits a grouped bar
     5	chart of false-positive rate (raw SR − adjusted SR) per mode, split by

    17

    22	
    23	MODES = ["DOM", "SoM", "Vision", "P-text", "P-prompt", "P-SoM"]

    25	    "DOM": "#4c78a8", "SoM": "#f58518", "Vision": "#54a24b",
    26	    "P-text": "#e45756", "P-prompt": "#9467bd", "P-SoM": "#b279a2",
    27	}

    30	def emit_placeholder(reason: str):

    33	            ha="center", va="center", fontsize=11, color="gray")
    34	    ax.set_axis_off()
    35	    fig.savefig(OUT, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")

    40	def main():
    41	    if not SRC.exists():
    42	        emit_placeholder(f"missing source {SRC.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    43	        return
    44	    data = json.loads(SRC.read_text())
    45	    rows = data.get("summary_table", [])
    46	    if not rows:
    47	        emit_placeholder("summary_table empty — run aggregators first")
    48	        return
    49	
    50	    # Group by (baseline, site) → mode → fp_pct
    51	    cells = {}
    52	    for r in rows:
    53	        bs = (r.get("baseline", "?"), r.get("site", "?"))

    59	    n_modes = len(MODES)
    60	
    61	    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, n_cells, figsize=(4.2 * n_cells, 4.5), sharey=True)
    62	    if n_cells == 1:
    63	        axes = [axes]
    64	
    65	    for ax, ck in zip(axes, cell_keys):

    69	        colors = [MODE_COLOR.get(m, "gray") for m in MODES]
    70	        bars = ax.bar(x, fp_pct, color=colors, edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.5)

    83	    fig.suptitle("False-positive rate per mode  (paper §1 0b — adjusted-SR hygiene)",

    88	    fig.tight_layout()

    99	    return sorted(ep_dir.glob("*_summary_v2.json"))
   100	
   101	
   102	def _list_steps_files(cond_dir: Path) -> List[Path]:
   103	    ep_dir = cond_dir / "episodes"
   104	    if not ep_dir.exists():
   105	        return []
   106	    return sorted(ep_dir.glob("*_steps_v2.jsonl"))
   107	
   108	
   109	def _task_id_from_filename(name: str) -> Optional[int]:
   110	    m = re.search(r"task_(\d+)", name)
   111	    return int(m.group(1)) if m else None
   112	
   113	
   114	def _sample_items(items: list, n: int) -> list:
   115	    if len(items) <= n:
   116	        return items
   117	    return random.sample(items, n)
   118	
   119	
   120	def _infer_benchmark(run_dir: Path) -> str:
   121	    """Infer benchmark from run directory path."""
   122	    parts = run_dir.parts
   123	    for i, p in enumerate(parts):
   124	        if p in ("visualwebarena", "webarena"):
   125	            return p
   126	    return "unknown"
   127	
   128	
   129	def _infer_site(run_dir: Path) -> str:
   130	    """Infer site from run_id."""
   131	    name = run_dir.name
   132	    for site in ("classifieds", "reddit", "shopping"):
   133	        if site in name:
   134	            return site
   135	    return "unknown"
   136	
   137	
   138	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   139	# Group 1: File existence
   140	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   141	
   142	
   143	def check_required_files(run_dir: Path) -> CheckResult:
   144	    """C01: Check that required analysis/condition files exist."""
   145	    missing = []
   146	    analysis = run_dir / "analysis"
   147	
   148	    # analysis_summary.json
   149	    if not (analysis / "analysis_summary.json").exists():
   150	        missing.append("analysis/analysis_summary.json")
   151	
   152	    # condition_metrics.csv
   153	    csv_path = analysis / "results" / "_overview" / "tables" / "condition_metrics.csv"
   154	    if not csv_path.exists():
   155	        missing.append("analysis/results/_overview/tables/condition_metrics.csv")
   156	
   157	    # Each condition's condition_summary_v2.json
   158	    for cond_dir in _condition_dirs(run_dir):
   159	        cs = cond_dir / "condition_summary_v2.json"
   160	        if not cs.exists():
   161	            missing.append(f"{cond_dir.name}/condition_summary_v2.json")
   162	
   163	    total_expected = 2 + len(list(_condition_dirs(run_dir)))
   164	    found = total_expected - len(missing)
   165	
   166	    if missing:
   167	        return CheckResult(
   168	            "C01", "Required files", "fail",
   169	            f"{found}/{total_expected} required files exist; missing: {', '.join(missing)}",
   170	            missing,
   171	        )
   172	    return CheckResult(
   173	        "C01", "Required files", "pass",
   174	        f"{found}/{total_expected} required files exist",
   175	    )
   176	
   177	
   178	def check_optional_files(run_dir: Path) -> CheckResult:
   179	    """C02: List missing optional files (INFO level)."""
   180	    analysis = run_dir / "analysis"
   181	    optional_paths = [
   182	        "digest/",
   183	        "results/cross_representation/",
   184	        "results/_overview/reports/statistical_tests.json",
   185	        "reason_diagnostics/condition_overview.csv",
   186	        "reason_diagnostics/condition_reason_summary.csv",
   187	        "reason_diagnostics/episode_reason_rows.csv",
   188	        "benchmark_noise/visual_lucky_hits.csv",
   189	        "benchmark_noise/na_reference_tasks.csv",
   190	        "signals/combined/tables/",
   191	        "reason_diagnostics/thought_trajectories.jsonl",
   192	        "reason_diagnostics/bucket_thought_samples.txt",
   193	    ]
   194	    missing = []
   195	    for p in optional_paths:
   196	        target = analysis / p
   197	        if not target.exists():
   198	            missing.append(p.rstrip("/"))
   199	
   200	    found = len(optional_paths) - len(missing)
   201	    if missing:
   202	        return CheckResult(
   203	            "C02", "Optional files", "info",
   204	            f"{found}/{len(optional_paths)} optional paths present; missing: {', '.join(missing)}",
   205	            missing,
   206	        )
   207	    return CheckResult(
   208	        "C02", "Optional files", "pass",
   209	        f"{found}/{len(optional_paths)} optional paths present",
   210	    )
   211	
   212	
   213	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   214	# Group 2: Run structure consistency
   215	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   216	
   217	
   218	def check_condition_completeness(run_dir: Path) -> CheckResult:
   219	    """C03: Check that all expected conditions exist."""
   220	    present = {d.name for d in _condition_dirs(run_dir)}
   221	    missing = [c for c in _EXPECTED_CONDITIONS if c not in present]
   222	    if missing:
   223	        return CheckResult(
   224	            "C03", "Condition completeness", "warn",
   225	            f"Missing conditions: {', '.join(missing)}",
   226	            missing,
   227	        )
   228	    return CheckResult(
   229	        "C03", "Condition completeness", "pass",
   230	        f"All {len(_EXPECTED_CONDITIONS)} expected conditions present",
   231	    )
   232	
   233	
   234	def check_observation_mode_mapping(run_dir: Path) -> CheckResult:
   235	    """C04: Verify observation_mode matches condition directory name."""
   236	    errors = []
   237	    for cond_name, expected_mode in _MODE_FROM_CONDITION.items():
   238	        cond_dir = run_dir / cond_name
   239	        if not cond_dir.exists():
   240	            continue
   241	        # Check condition_meta.json
   242	        meta = _load_json(cond_dir / "condition_meta.json")
   243	        if meta and meta.get("observation_mode") != expected_mode:
   244	            errors.append(f"{cond_name}/condition_meta.json: observation_mode={meta.get('observation_mode')} (expected {expected_mode})")
   245	        # Check condition_summary_v2.json
   246	        summary = _load_json(cond_dir / "condition_summary_v2.json")
   247	        if summary and summary.get("observation_mode") != expected_mode:
   248	            errors.append(f"{cond_name}/condition_summary_v2.json: observation_mode={summary.get('observation_mode')} (expected {expected_mode})")
   249	
   250	    if errors:
   251	        return CheckResult(
   252	            "C04", "Observation mode mapping", "fail",
   253	            f"Mismatches: {'; '.join(errors)}",
   254	            errors,
   255	        )
   256	    return CheckResult(
   257	        "C04", "Observation mode mapping", "pass",
   258	        "All observation_mode fields match condition directory names",
   259	    )
   260	
   261	
   262	def check_module_flags(run_dir: Path) -> CheckResult:
   263	    """C05: Phase 1 module_flags should all be false."""
   264	    issues = []
   265	    for cond_dir in _condition_dirs(run_dir):
   266	        meta = _load_json(cond_dir / "condition_meta.json")
   267	        if not meta:
   268	            continue
   269	        modules = meta.get("modules", {})
   270	        enabled = [k for k, v in modules.items() if v]
   271	        if enabled:
   272	            issues.append(f"{cond_dir.name}: {', '.join(enabled)} are True")
   273	
   274	    if issues:
   275	        return CheckResult(
   276	            "C05", "Module flags consistency", "warn",
   277	            f"Expected all false in Phase 1: {'; '.join(issues)}",
   278	            issues,
   279	        )
   280	    return CheckResult(
   281	        "C05", "Module flags consistency", "pass",
   282	        "All module_flags are false (correct for Phase 1)",
   283	    )
   284	
   285	
   286	def check_benchmark_field(run_dir: Path, sample_size: int) -> CheckResult:
   287	    """C06: Sampled step/summary benchmark field matches run directory path."""
   288	    expected_benchmark = _infer_benchmark(run_dir)
   289	    if expected_benchmark == "unknown":
   290	        return CheckResult(
   291	            "C06", "Benchmark field consistency", "skip",
   292	            "Cannot infer benchmark from run directory path",
   293	        )
   294	
   295	    errors = []
   296	    for cond_dir in _condition_dirs(run_dir):
   297	        summaries = _list_summaries(cond_dir)
   298	        for sf in _sample_items(summaries, sample_size):
   299	            data = _load_json(sf)
   300	            if data and data.get("benchmark") != expected_benchmark:
   301	                errors.append(f"{sf.name}: benchmark={data.get('benchmark')}")
   302	
   303	        steps_files = _list_steps_files(cond_dir)
   304	        for stf in _sample_items(steps_files, sample_size):
   305	            lines = read_jsonl_dedup(stf)
   306	            if lines and lines[0].get("benchmark") != expected_benchmark:
   307	                errors.append(f"{stf.name}: benchmark={lines[0].get('benchmark')}")
   308	
   309	    if errors:
   310	        return CheckResult(
   311	            "C06", "Benchmark field consistency", "fail",
   312	            f"Mismatches (expected {expected_benchmark}): {'; '.join(errors[:10])}",
   313	            errors,
   314	        )
   315	    return CheckResult(
   316	        "C06", "Benchmark field consistency", "pass",
   317	        f"All sampled records have benchmark={expected_benchmark}",
   318	    )

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""[Outcome supporting] Meta-analytic forest plot — per-arm pooled estimate
     3	+ I² + Q + per-cell weight squares.
     4	
     5	Reads `results/phantom_paper/meta_phantom_lift.csv` (T0c output) +
     6	`results/phantom_paper/phantom_lift.csv` (T0a output, for per-cell rows).
     7	Renders 3 panels (P-text / P-SoM / P-prompt) with classical forest convention:
     8	
     9	- Per-cell row: square sized by RE weight (% of pooled), horizontal 95% CI line
    10	- Pooled row at bottom: diamond (center = pooled estimate, width = pooled 95% CI)
    11	- I² + Q + p_Q + τ² annotation in panel
    12	- Vertical line at lift = 0 (null)
    13	- TOST equivalence band shaded ±0.5pp
    14	
    15	Output: `results/phantom_paper/figures/fig_meta_forest.png`
    16	
    17	T0d of `docs/reference/EVIDENCE_LAYER_AUDIT.md` action queue.
    18	
    19	Difference from `fig_forest_drop_one.py` (T0b): this adds the meta-pooled
    20	diamond + heterogeneity statistics + weight-sized squares (classical forest
    21	convention). T0b is per-cell-only, no pooling.
    22	"""

    24

    41	ARMS = [
    42	    ("4psom",    "4psom_vs_3",    "P-SoM drop-in",    "#b279a2", "HERO"),
    43	    ("4pdom",    "4pdom_vs_3",    "P-text drop-in",   "#9e6da8", "ABLATION"),
    44	    ("4pprompt", "4pprompt_vs_3", "P-prompt drop-in", "#9467bd", "ABLATION"),
    45	]
    46	
    47	ROLE_BADGE = {
    48	    "HERO":     "DEPLOYMENT HERO (H1, gating)",

    50	}
    51	ROLE_DIAMOND_STYLE = {
    52	    "HERO":     dict(facecolor="#000000", edgecolor="#000000", linewidth=1.2, alpha=1.0),
    53	    "ABLATION": dict(facecolor="#cccccc", edgecolor="#444444", linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.7),
    54	}
    55	
    56	TOST_DELTA_PP = 0.5

    59	def _f(x):
    60	    if x is None or x == "" or x == "None":

    62	    return float(x)
    63	
    64	
    65	def load_per_cell(arm_csv_prefix: str) -> list[dict]:
    66	    rows = []
    67	    with LIFT_CSV.open() as f:
    68	        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    69	        for r in reader:
    70	            theta = _f(r.get(f"lift_{arm_csv_prefix}_vs_3_pp"))
    71	            ci_lo = _f(r.get(f"lift_{arm_csv_prefix}_vs_3_ci95_lo_pp"))
    72	            ci_hi = _f(r.get(f"lift_{arm_csv_prefix}_vs_3_ci95_hi_pp"))
    73	            if theta is None or ci_lo is None or ci_hi is None:
    74	                continue
    75	            se = (ci_hi - ci_lo) / (2 * 1.96)
    76	            if se <= 0:
    77	                continue
    78	            rows.append({
    79	                "label": f"{r['baseline']} {r['site']}",
    80	                "theta": theta,
    81	                "ci_lo": ci_lo,
    82	                "ci_hi": ci_hi,
    83	                "se": se,
    84	            })
    85	    return rows

    88	def load_meta(arm_code: str) -> dict | None:
    89	    if not META_CSV.exists():
    90	        return None
    91	    with META_CSV.open() as f:

    98	def draw_arm_panel(ax: plt.Axes, arm_csv_prefix: str, meta_arm_code: str,
    99	                   label: str, color: str, role: str = "ABLATION") -> None:
   100	    cells = load_per_cell(arm_csv_prefix)
   101	    meta = load_meta(meta_arm_code)
   102	
   103	    # TOST band + null line
   104	    ax.axvspan(-TOST_DELTA_PP, TOST_DELTA_PP, alpha=0.18, color="#888888", zorder=0)
   105	    ax.axvline(0, color="#444444", linewidth=0.8, linestyle="--", zorder=1)
   106	
   107	    if not cells:
   108	        ax.text(0.5, 0.5, f"no cells for {label}", ha="center", va="center",
   109	                transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=10, color="#888888", style="italic")
   110	        ax.set_yticks([])
   111	        ax.set_title(label, fontsize=11, fontweight="bold", color=color)
   112	        return
   113	
   114	    # RE weight per cell (use meta's tau² if available, else FE weights)
   115	    tau2 = float(meta["tau2"]) if meta and meta.get("tau2") not in (None, "") else 0.0
   116	    var_star = np.array([c["se"] ** 2 + tau2 for c in cells])
   117	    w_star = 1.0 / var_star
   118	    weights = w_star / w_star.sum()
   119	
   120	    n_rows = len(cells) + (1 if meta else 0)  # cells + diamond row
   121	    y_positions = np.arange(n_rows)
   122	    cell_y = y_positions[:len(cells)]
   123	
   124	    # Per-cell rows: weight-sized squares + CI line
   125	    for i, c in enumerate(cells):
   126	        # CI line
   127	        ax.plot([c["ci_lo"], c["ci_hi"]], [cell_y[i], cell_y[i]],
   128	                color=color, linewidth=1.5, zorder=2)
   129	        # Square sized by weight (visual area ∝ weight)
   130	        size = 80 + 320 * weights[i]  # 80-400 size range
   131	        ax.scatter(c["theta"], cell_y[i], marker="s", s=size,
   132	                   facecolor=color, edgecolor="#222222", linewidth=0.8, zorder=3)
   133	
   134	    # Pooled diamond — HERO = filled black; ABLATION = gray outlined
   135	    if meta:
   136	        re_y = y_positions[-1]
   137	        re_theta = float(meta["theta_re"])
   138	        re_ci_lo = float(meta["ci_lo"])
   139	        re_ci_hi = float(meta["ci_hi"])
   140	        diamond_x = [re_ci_lo, re_theta, re_ci_hi, re_theta]
   141	        diamond_y = [re_y, re_y - 0.28, re_y, re_y + 0.28]
   142	        style = ROLE_DIAMOND_STYLE[role]
   143	        ax.fill(diamond_x, diamond_y, **style, zorder=4)
   144	        # Outline only for ABLATION (already drawn by fill, but emphasize edge)
   145	        if role == "ABLATION":
   146	            ax.plot(diamond_x + [diamond_x[0]], diamond_y + [diamond_y[0]],
   147	                    color=style["edgecolor"], linewidth=style["linewidth"], zorder=4)
   148	        # Pooled summary line at zero
   149	        ax.axhline(re_y - 0.65, color="#cccccc", linewidth=0.5, linestyle=":")
   150	
   151	    # Y-tick labels
   152	    yticks = list(cell_y)
   153	    yticklabels = [c["label"] for c in cells]
   154	    if meta:
   155	        yticks.append(y_positions[-1])
   156	        k = meta["k_cells"]
   157	        yticklabels.append(f"Pooled (RE, k={k})")
   158	    ax.set_yticks(yticks)
   159	    ax.set_yticklabels(yticklabels, fontsize=9)
   160	    ax.invert_yaxis()
   161	
   162	    # Annotations: per-cell lift + weight; pooled lift + I² + Q
   163	    x_anno = ax.get_xlim()[1] if False else None  # set after autoscale
   164	    for i, c in enumerate(cells):
   165	        ax.text(c["ci_hi"] + 0.15, cell_y[i],
   166	                f"  {c['theta']:+.2f}pp [{c['ci_lo']:.2f},{c['ci_hi']:.2f}] "
   167	                f"  w={weights[i]*100:.0f}%",
   168	                va="center", fontsize=8.0, color="#333333")
   169	    if meta:
   170	        I2 = float(meta["I2"])
   171	        Q = float(meta["Q"])
   172	        df = int(meta["df"])
   173	        p_Q = meta.get("p_Q")
   174	        p_Q_str = (f"{float(p_Q):.3f}" if p_Q not in (None, "") else "—")
   175	        re_theta = float(meta["theta_re"])
   176	        re_ci_lo = float(meta["ci_lo"])
   177	        re_ci_hi = float(meta["ci_hi"])
   178	        p_re_holm = meta.get("p_re_holm", "")
   179	        holm_str = (f"Holm p={float(p_re_holm):.3f}" if p_re_holm not in (None, "")
   180	                    else "")
   181	        ax.text(re_ci_hi + 0.15, y_positions[-1],
   182	                f"  {re_theta:+.2f}pp [{re_ci_lo:.2f},{re_ci_hi:.2f}]  "
   183	                f"I²={I2:.0f}%  Q({df})={Q:.2f} p={p_Q_str}  {holm_str}",
   184	                va="center", fontsize=8.0, color="#222222", fontweight="bold")
   185	
   186	    # Title with role badge
   187	    title_color = "#000000" if role == "HERO" else color

   189	    ax.set_title(f"{label}  —  {ROLE_BADGE[role]}", fontsize=11,

   191	    # HERO panel gets a stronger frame to emphasize epistemic priority

   196	    ax.grid(axis="x", color="#dddddd", linewidth=0.6, zorder=0)

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""[Outcome supporting] Forest plot — per-arm drop-one lift across cells.
     3	
     4	Reads `results/phantom_paper/phantom_lift.csv` (T0a-augmented with Holm/BH/TOST).
     5	Renders 3 stacked panels (P-text / P-SoM / P-prompt), each showing per-cell
     6	drop-one lift point estimate + raw 95% bootstrap CI + Holm-adjusted-significance
     7	marker + TOST equivalence band (δ=0.5pp).
     8	
     9	Output: `results/phantom_paper/figures/fig_forest_drop_one.png`
    10	
    11	Per the pre-registered SECONDARY family (m = N_cells × 3 arms), Holm-Bonferroni
    12	adjusted p-value gates the sig marker. Raw 95% CI is shown as the visual primary
    13	because Holm-adjusted CI is rank-dependent within family and confuses the reader;
    14	sig marker carries the multi-comparison gating.
    15	
    16	T0b of `docs/reference/EVIDENCE_LAYER_AUDIT.md` action queue.
    17	"""
    18	from __future__ import annotations
    19	
    20	import csv
    21	import sys
    22	from pathlib import Path
    23	
    24	import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
    25	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    26	import numpy as np
    27	
    28	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
    29	CSV_IN = ROOT / "results/phantom_paper/phantom_lift.csv"
    30	OUT = ROOT / "results/phantom_paper/figures/fig_forest_drop_one.png"
    31	
    32	# Per-arm config: (csv arm prefix, display label, color)
    33	ARMS = [
    34	    ("4pdom",    "P-text",   "#9e6da8"),
    35	    ("4psom",    "P-SoM",    "#b279a2"),
    36	    ("4pprompt", "P-prompt", "#9467bd"),
    37	]
    38	
    39	TOST_DELTA_PP = 0.5
    40	SIG_ALPHA = 0.05
    41	
    42	
    43	def _f(x):
    44	    """CSV float parser tolerating empty / 'None' strings."""
    45	    if x is None or x == "" or x == "None":
    46	        return None
    47	    return float(x)
    48	
    49	
    50	def load_rows() -> list[dict]:
    51	    if not CSV_IN.exists():
    52	        sys.exit(f"missing {CSV_IN}; run scripts/analysis/aggregate_phantom_lift.py first")
    53	    with CSV_IN.open() as f:
    54	        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    55	        return list(reader)
    56	
    57	
    58	def cell_label(row: dict) -> str:
    59	    return f"{row['baseline']} {row['site']}"

    62	def draw_arm_panel(ax: plt.Axes, rows: list[dict], arm_code: str, label: str,
    63	                   color: str) -> None:
    64	    """One panel: y = cells, x = lift (pp), per-cell point + CI + sig."""
    65	    # Filter cells that have data for this arm
    66	    plotted = []
    67	    for r in rows:
    68	        lift = _f(r.get(f"lift_{arm_code}_vs_3_pp"))
    69	        if lift is None:
    70	            continue
    71	        ci_lo = _f(r.get(f"lift_{arm_code}_vs_3_ci95_lo_pp"))
    72	        ci_hi = _f(r.get(f"lift_{arm_code}_vs_3_ci95_hi_pp"))
    73	        holm_p = _f(r.get(f"mcnemar_{arm_code}_vs_3_p_holm"))
    74	        tost_p = _f(r.get(f"tost_{arm_code}_vs_3_p"))
    75	        h = _f(r.get(f"cohen_h_{arm_code}_vs_3"))
    76	        plotted.append({
    77	            "label": cell_label(r),
    78	            "lift": lift,
    79	            "ci_lo": ci_lo if ci_lo is not None else lift,
    80	            "ci_hi": ci_hi if ci_hi is not None else lift,
    81	            "holm_p": holm_p,
    82	            "tost_p": tost_p,
    83	            "h": h,
    84	        })
    85	
    86	    # TOST equivalence band (δ=0.5pp): shade [-δ, +δ]
    87	    ax.axvspan(-TOST_DELTA_PP, TOST_DELTA_PP, alpha=0.18, color="#888888", zorder=0,
    88	               label=f"TOST equivalence band (±{TOST_DELTA_PP}pp)")
    89	    # Null line
    90	    ax.axvline(0, color="#444444", linewidth=0.8, linestyle="--", zorder=1)
    91	
    92	    if not plotted:
    93	        ax.text(0.5, 0.5, f"no cells with {label} data yet",
    94	                ha="center", va="center", transform=ax.transAxes,
    95	                fontsize=10, color="#888888", style="italic")
    96	        ax.set_yticks([])
    97	        ax.set_title(f"{label} drop-one lift (vs 3-mode)", fontsize=11,
    98	                     fontweight="bold", color=color)
    99	        return
   100	
   101	    y = np.arange(len(plotted))
   102	    lifts = np.array([p["lift"] for p in plotted])
   103	    err_lo = np.array([max(0.0, p["lift"] - p["ci_lo"]) for p in plotted])
   104	    err_hi = np.array([max(0.0, p["ci_hi"] - p["lift"]) for p in plotted])
   105	
   106	    # Holm-significant cells = filled, non-sig = open marker
   107	    sig_mask = np.array([
   108	        (p["holm_p"] is not None and p["holm_p"] < SIG_ALPHA) for p in plotted
   109	    ])
   110	
   111	    # Error bars (raw 95% CI), all cells
   112	    ax.errorbar(
   113	        lifts, y, xerr=[err_lo, err_hi],
   114	        fmt="none", ecolor=color, elinewidth=2.0, capsize=4, capthick=1.5, zorder=2,
   115	    )
   116	    # Filled markers (sig)
   117	    if sig_mask.any():
   118	        ax.scatter(lifts[sig_mask], y[sig_mask], s=110, marker="o",
   119	                   facecolor=color, edgecolor="#222222", linewidth=1.2, zorder=3,
   120	                   label="Holm-adj p < 0.05")
   121	    # Open markers (non-sig)
   122	    if (~sig_mask).any():
   123	        ax.scatter(lifts[~sig_mask], y[~sig_mask], s=110, marker="o",
   124	                   facecolor="white", edgecolor=color, linewidth=1.5, zorder=3,
   125	                   label="Holm-adj p ≥ 0.05")
   126	
   127	    # Annotations: lift value + Holm p + Cohen's h
   128	    for i, p in enumerate(plotted):
   129	        h_txt = f"h={p['h']:.3f}" if p["h"] is not None else ""
   130	        holm_txt = (f"Holm p={p['holm_p']:.3f}"
   131	                    if p["holm_p"] is not None else "Holm p=—")
   132	        annot = f"  {p['lift']:+.2f}pp  ({holm_txt}, {h_txt})"
   133	        ax.text(p["ci_hi"] + 0.15, i, annot, va="center", fontsize=8.0,
   134	                color="#333333")
   135	
   136	    ax.set_yticks(y)
   137	    ax.set_yticklabels([p["label"] for p in plotted], fontsize=9)
   138	    ax.invert_yaxis()  # First cell on top
   139	    ax.set_title(f"{label} drop-one lift (vs 3-mode)", fontsize=11,
   140	                 fontweight="bold", color=color)
   141	    ax.grid(axis="x", color="#dddddd", linewidth=0.6, zorder=0)
   142	    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
   143	
   144	
   145	def main() -> None:
   146	    OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   147	    rows = load_rows()
   148	    plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 10, "figure.dpi": 150})
   149	    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(ARMS), 1, figsize=(11.5, 7.5), sharex=True)
   150	    if len(ARMS) == 1:
   151	        axes = [axes]
   152	    for ax, (code, label, color) in zip(axes, ARMS):
   153	        draw_arm_panel(ax, rows, code, label, color)
   154	    axes[-1].set_xlabel("Drop-one lift (pp; vs 3-mode oracle = DOM ∪ SoM ∪ Vision)",
   155	                        fontsize=10)
   156	
   157	    # Determine x range based on data + leave annotation room
   158	    all_lifts = []
   159	    all_ci = []
   160	    for r in rows:
   161	        for code, _, _ in ARMS:
   162	            ci_hi = _f(r.get(f"lift_{code}_vs_3_ci95_hi_pp"))
   163	            ci_lo = _f(r.get(f"lift_{code}_vs_3_ci95_lo_pp"))
   164	            if ci_hi is not None:
   165	                all_ci.append(ci_hi)
   166	            if ci_lo is not None:
   167	                all_ci.append(ci_lo)
   168	            lift = _f(r.get(f"lift_{code}_vs_3_pp"))
   169	            if lift is not None:
   170	                all_lifts.append(lift)
   171	    if all_ci:
   172	        x_max = max(all_ci) + 6.0  # leave room for annotation
   173	        x_min = min(min(all_ci), -1.0)
   174	        for ax in axes:
   175	            ax.set_xlim(x_min, x_max)
   176	
   177	    # Shared legend: build from first panel
   178	    handles, labels = axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
   179	    # Dedup
   180	    seen = set()
   181	    legend_items = []
   182	    for h, l in zip(handles, labels):
   183	        if l not in seen:
   184	            seen.add(l)
   185	            legend_items.append((h, l))
   186	    if legend_items:
   187	        fig.legend([h for h, _ in legend_items], [l for _, l in legend_items],
   188	                    loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.02), ncol=3,
   189	                    frameon=False, fontsize=9)
   190	
   191	    fig.suptitle(
   192	        "Forest plot — per-arm drop-one lift across cells (raw 95% bootstrap CI; Holm-gated sig)",
   193	        fontsize=12.5, fontweight="bold",
   194	    )
   195	    fig.text(
   196	        0.5, 0.02,
   197	        "Filled marker = Holm-adjusted McNemar p < 0.05 within SECONDARY family "
   198	        "(m = N_cells × 3 arms). Open marker = Holm p ≥ 0.05. Gray band = TOST "
   199	        f"equivalence margin ±{TOST_DELTA_PP}pp (effects within band are practically zero).",
   200	        ha="center", fontsize=8.5, color="#555555",
   201	    )
   202	    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.05, 1, 0.94))
   203	    fig.savefig(OUT, bbox_inches="tight")
   204	    print(OUT)
   205	
   206	
   207	if __name__ == "__main__":
   208	    main()

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""[Outcome 0c + 0d] Outcome dimension — routing oracle lift and task-pool Jaccard.
     3	
     4	Outputs:
     5	- results/phantom_paper/phantom_lift.csv
     6	- results/phantom_paper/phantom_lift.md
     7	
     8	Outcome 0c: 3-mode to 4/5-mode oracle lift and significance tests.
     9	Outcome 0d: P-text↔P-SoM task-pool Jaccard Scenario C sentinel.
    10	
    11	See docs/checkpoints/paper_planning.md §3 Outcome dimension framework.
    12	
    13	Aggregate phantom routing lift across (baseline, site) cells.
    14	
    15	For each cell with all 5 modes (DOM / SoM / Vision / P-text / P-SoM) present:
    16	  - Compute 3-mode oracle ceiling (DOM ∪ SoM ∪ Vision)
    17	  - Compute 5-mode oracle ceiling (+ P-text + P-SoM)
    18	  - Routing lift = 5-mode - 3-mode oracle SR (pp)
    19	  - 95% bootstrap CI on lift (n=1000 task resamples)
    20	  - Decomposition: P-text-only, P-SoM-only, both-add-same contributions
    21	
    22	Outputs (results/phantom_paper/):
    23	  - phantom_lift.csv          (one row per (baseline, site, decomposition))
    24	  - phantom_lift_summary.md   (paper-ready table for Section 1/4 hook)
    25	
    26	Usage:
    27	    python3 scripts/analysis/aggregate_phantom_lift.py [--cells <baseline:site:...>]
    28	
    29	Default cells = paper-grade clean B0 cls/red. B1 cells included if all 5 modes
    30	have data (>= 50 ep each). Partial cells use the common observed-task universe.
    31	"""
    32	from __future__ import annotations

    92	def load(d: Path) -> tuple[set[int], set[int]]:
    93	    """Returns (succ_set, observed_set)."""
    94	    s, o = set(), set()
    95	    if not d.exists():
    96	        return s, o
    97	    # F05 audit fix 2026-05-09: track corrupt summary count instead of
    98	    # silently dropping; warn at end of cell. Set P79_STRICT=1 to fail.
    99	    n_corrupt = 0
   100	    for p in sorted(d.glob("*_summary_v2.json")):
   101	        m = re.search(r"task_(\d+)", p.name)
   102	        if not m:
   103	            continue
   104	        tid = int(m.group(1))
   105	        o.add(tid)
   106	        try:
   107	            rec = json.loads(p.read_text())
   108	        except Exception as _e:
   109	            n_corrupt += 1
   110	            continue
   111	        if rec.get("adjusted_success", rec.get("success", False)):
   112	            s.add(tid)
   113	    if n_corrupt > 0:
   114	        msg = (
   115	            f"  [F05] {d}: {n_corrupt} corrupt summary file(s) skipped "
   116	            "(could change oracle union + pp lift). Set P79_STRICT=1 to fail."
   117	        )
   118	        if os.environ.get("P79_STRICT", "").lower() in ("1", "true", "yes"):
   119	            raise RuntimeError(msg)
   120	        print(f"WARNING: {msg}")
   121	    return s, o

   124	def bootstrap_lift_ci(in_3: np.ndarray, in_5: np.ndarray, B: int = 1000, seed: int = 42
   125	                      ) -> tuple[float, float]:
   126	    """Bootstrap 95% CI on (5-mode oracle SR - 3-mode oracle SR)."""
   127	    n = len(in_3)
   128	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
   129	    lifts = np.empty(B)
   130	    for b in range(B):
   131	        idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=n)
   132	        lifts[b] = 100 * (int(in_5[idx].sum()) - int(in_3[idx].sum())) / n
   133	    return float(np.quantile(lifts, 0.025)), float(np.quantile(lifts, 0.975))

   136	def cohen_h(p1: float, p2: float) -> float:
   137	    """Cohen's h effect size between two proportions p1, p2 ∈ [0, 1].
   138	
   139	    h = 2 * (arcsin(√p1) - arcsin(√p2))
   140	
   141	    Interpretation: |h|<0.2 small, 0.2-0.5 medium, 0.5-0.8 large, >0.8 huge.
   142	    Sign indicates direction (p1 > p2 → h > 0).
   143	    """
   144	    p1 = max(0.0, min(1.0, p1))
   145	    p2 = max(0.0, min(1.0, p2))
   146	    return 2 * (math.asin(math.sqrt(p1)) - math.asin(math.sqrt(p2)))
   147	
   148	
   149	def cohen_h_label(h: float) -> str:
   150	    a = abs(h)
   151	    if a < 0.2:
   152	        return "small"
   153	    if a < 0.5:
   154	        return "medium"
   155	    if a < 0.8:
   156	        return "large"
   157	    return "huge"
   158

   160	def wilcoxon_signed_rank(in_a: np.ndarray, in_b: np.ndarray) -> tuple[Optional[float], Optional[float]]:
   161	    """Wilcoxon signed-rank test on paired binary task outcomes (a vs b).
   162	
   163	    For binary outcomes diff ∈ {-1, 0, +1}; scipy drops zero diffs. When set b
   164	    ⊇ set a (e.g. 5-mode oracle ⊇ 3-mode oracle), all non-zero diffs are
   165	    positive (b solves task that a doesn't) → test reduces to one-sided
   166	    binomial (sign test). Returns (statistic, p_two_sided) or (None, None) if
   167	    scipy unavailable / undefined.
   168	    """
   169	    if not HAS_SCIPY:
   170	        return None, None
   171	    diffs = in_b.astype(int) - in_a.astype(int)
   172	    nonzero = diffs[diffs != 0]
   173	    if len(nonzero) == 0:
   174	        return None, 1.0  # no difference, p = 1
   175	    try:
   176	        with warnings.catch_warnings():
   177	            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
   178	            stat, p = sp_stats.wilcoxon(diffs, zero_method="wilcox", alternative="two-sided")
   179	        return float(stat), float(p)
   180	    except Exception:
   181	        return None, None
   182	
   183	
   184	def mcnemar_exact_one_sided(in_a: np.ndarray, in_b: np.ndarray) -> Optional[float]:
   185	    """McNemar exact one-sided p-value: H1 = b > a (b adds tasks a misses).
   186	
   187	    For monotonic case (b ⊇ a), discordant b-only count = sum(b - a > 0),
   188	    a-only count = 0. Exact binomial: p = 0.5^(b_only).
   189	    """
   190	    if not HAS_SCIPY:
   191	        return None
   192	    a = in_a.astype(int); b = in_b.astype(int)
   193	    a_only = int(((a > b)).sum())
   194	    b_only = int(((b > a)).sum())
   195	    n_disc = a_only + b_only
   196	    if n_disc == 0:
   197	        return 1.0
   198	    # one-sided: H1 = b > a
   199	    return float(sp_stats.binom.cdf(a_only, n_disc, 0.5))
   200	
   201	
   202	def bootstrap_unique_count_ci(in_a: np.ndarray, in_b: np.ndarray,
   203	                              B: int = 1000, seed: int = 42, ci: float = 0.95
   204	                              ) -> tuple[int, float, float]:
   205	    """Bootstrap CI on |a ∖ b| count: tasks where a solves but b doesn't.
   206	
   207	    H3 structural claim test: arm a contributes tasks NOT solved by arm b.
   208	    If lower CI bound > 0, "a has unique non-overlap with b" sig at 1-ci level.
   209	
   210	    Used per-cell for:
   211	      P-text ∖ P-SoM unique count (axis 1 structural evidence)
   212	      P-prompt ∖ P-SoM unique count (axis 2 structural evidence)
   213	    """
   214	    n = len(in_a)
   215	    if n == 0 or len(in_b) != n:
   216	        return 0, 0.0, 0.0
   217	    a = in_a.astype(bool)
   218	    b = in_b.astype(bool)
   219	    observed = int((a & ~b).sum())
   220	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
   220	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
   221	    counts = np.empty(B)
   222	    for r in range(B):
   223	        idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=n)
   224	        counts[r] = int((a[idx] & ~b[idx]).sum())
   225	    alpha = (1 - ci) / 2
   226	    return observed, float(np.quantile(counts, alpha)), float(np.quantile(counts, 1 - alpha))
   227

   229	def bootstrap_tost_equivalence_p(in_a: np.ndarray, in_b: np.ndarray,
   230	                                  delta_pp: float = 1.0, B: int = 1000, seed: int = 42
   231	                                  ) -> Optional[float]:
   232	    """Bootstrap TOST (Two One-Sided Tests) p-value for **equivalence** test.
   233	
   234	    H0: |true lift| >= δ          (effect is meaningful in either direction)
   235	    H1: |true lift| < δ           (effect equivalent to zero within margin)
   236	
   237	    Two one-sided tests:
   238	      H0_lower:  lift <= -δ  → reject if bootstrap dist mostly above -δ
   239	                              p_lower = P(boot_lift <= -δ); small p_lower
   240	                              ⇒ evidence rejects "effect <= -δ"
   241	      H0_upper:  lift >= +δ  → reject if bootstrap dist mostly below +δ
   242	                              p_upper = P(boot_lift >= +δ); small p_upper
   243	                              ⇒ evidence rejects "effect >= +δ"
   244	
   245	    TOST p = max(p_lower, p_upper).
   246	    **If max(p_lower, p_upper) < α, equivalence is ACCEPTED** — both
   247	    one-sided tests reject, so the effect is bounded inside (-δ, +δ).
   248	
   249	    F03 audit fix 2026-05-09: δ default = 1.0pp (was 0.5). Matches
   250	    `preregistration.md §4` lock "TOST equivalence margin δ = 1.0pp".
   251	
   252	    F04 audit fix 2026-05-09: renamed from `bootstrap_tost_p`; clarified
   253	    docstring (previous wording said "equivalence rejected when max < α"
   254	    which inverts the conclusion). Strong positive lift gives p_upper≈1
   255	    correctly (effect is outside +δ equivalence margin), so equivalence
   256	    is correctly NOT accepted.
   257	
   258	    For the **nonzero / one-sided directional** test (the phantom-lift
   259	    hypothesis "lift > 0"), use `bootstrap_one_sided_nonzero_p()` below.
   260	    """
   261	    if len(in_a) != len(in_b):
   262	        return None
   263	    n = len(in_a)
   264	    if n == 0:
   265	        return None
   266	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
   267	    lifts = np.empty(B)
   268	    for b in range(B):
   269	        idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=n)
   270	        lifts[b] = 100 * (int(in_b[idx].sum()) - int(in_a[idx].sum())) / n
   271	    p_lower = float(np.mean(lifts <= -delta_pp))
   272	    p_upper = float(np.mean(lifts >= delta_pp))
   273	    return max(p_lower, p_upper)
   274	
   275	
   276	# F04 audit fix 2026-05-09: alias preserves backward-compat callers; new
   277	# code should use the renamed `bootstrap_tost_equivalence_p()`.
   278	bootstrap_tost_p = bootstrap_tost_equivalence_p
   279	
   280	
   281	def bootstrap_one_sided_nonzero_p(in_a: np.ndarray, in_b: np.ndarray,
   282	                                   B: int = 1000, seed: int = 42,
   283	                                   alternative: str = "greater"
   284	                                   ) -> Optional[float]:
   285	    """Bootstrap one-sided p-value for the directional phantom-lift claim.
   286	
   287	    H0: lift = 0     (no phantom-routing benefit)
   288	    H1: lift > 0     (alternative='greater', default — primary paper claim)
   289	       or lift < 0   (alternative='less')
   290	
   291	    p = fraction of bootstrap resamples where lift contradicts H1
   292	        (alternative='greater' → fraction with lift <= 0)
   293	        (alternative='less' → fraction with lift >= 0)
   294	
   295	    F04 audit fix 2026-05-09: added as the correct test for the paper's
   296	    phantom-lift > 0 claim; the equivalence-style TOST in
   297	    `bootstrap_tost_equivalence_p()` is for the separate "lift is bounded
   298	    inside ±δ" claim and should NOT be substituted for nonzero detection.
   299	    """
   300	    if len(in_a) != len(in_b) or len(in_a) == 0:
   301	        return None
   302	    n = len(in_a)
   303	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
   304	    lifts = np.empty(B)
   305	    for b in range(B):
   306	        idx = rng.integers(0, n, size=n)
   307	        lifts[b] = 100 * (int(in_b[idx].sum()) - int(in_a[idx].sum())) / n
   308	    if alternative == "greater":
   309	        return float(np.mean(lifts <= 0.0))
   310	    elif alternative == "less":
   311	        return float(np.mean(lifts >= 0.0))
   312	    else:
   313	        raise ValueError(f"alternative must be 'greater' or 'less', got {alternative}")
   314	
   315	
   316	def bonferroni_adjust(pvals: list) -> list:
   317	    """Bonferroni: p_adj = min(1, m * p_raw); None entries pass-through."""
   318	    m = sum(1 for p in pvals if p is not None)
   319	    if m == 0:
   320	        return list(pvals)
   321	    return [min(1.0, m * p) if p is not None else None for p in pvals]
   322	
   323	
   324	def holm_bonferroni_adjust(pvals: list) -> list:
   325	    """Holm-Bonferroni step-down (Holm 1979): less conservative than Bonferroni
   326	    while still controlling family-wise error rate at α.
   327	
   328	    Sort non-None p-values ascending; the k-th smallest gets multiplied by
   329	    (m - k + 1) where m = number of non-None tests; running max enforces
   330	    monotonicity.
   331	    """
   332	    indexed = [(i, p) for i, p in enumerate(pvals) if p is not None]
   333	    indexed.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
   334	    m = len(indexed)
   335	    out: list = [None] * len(pvals)
   336	    prev = 0.0
   337	    for k, (i, p) in enumerate(indexed):
   338	        adj = min(1.0, max(prev, p * (m - k)))
   339	        out[i] = adj
   340	        prev = adj
   341	    return out
   342	
   343	
   344	def bh_fdr_adjust(pvals: list) -> list:
   345	    """Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjusted q-values (BH 1995).
   346	
   347	    Less conservative than FWER methods; controls expected proportion of false
   348	    discoveries among rejections rather than family-wise error rate.
   349	    """
   350	    indexed = [(i, p) for i, p in enumerate(pvals) if p is not None]
   351	    indexed.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
   352	    m = len(indexed)
   353	    out: list = [None] * len(pvals)
   354	    prev = 1.0
   355	    for k in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
   356	        i, p = indexed[k]
   357	        rank = k + 1
   358	        adj = min(prev, p * m / rank)
   359	        out[i] = min(1.0, adj)
   360	        prev = out[i]
   361	    return out
   362

   364	def analyze_cell(cell: dict) -> Optional[dict]:
   365	    """Compute phantom lift for a single (baseline, site) cell.
   366	
   367	    Required modes: DOM, SoM, Vision, P-SoM. P-text and P-prompt are optional —
   368	    when absent, dependent oracle/lift columns are emitted as None (CSV blank).
   369	
   370	    Returns None if any required mode missing or below MIN_EP_FOR_CELL.
   371	    """
   372	    succ, obs = {}, {}
   373	    for mode, ep_dir in cell["modes"].items():
   374	        s, o = load(ep_dir)
   375	        if len(o) < MIN_EP_FOR_CELL:
   376	            # Skip undersized modes silently; allow rest of cell to still build.
   377	            # P-prompt cell may be partial (e.g. 127/210); keep it if it meets MIN.
   378	            continue
   379	        succ[mode] = s
   380	        obs[mode] = o
   381	
   382	    required = ("DOM", "SoM", "Vision", "P-SoM")
   383	    if any(m not in succ for m in required):
   384	        return None
   385	    has_pdom = "P-text" in succ
   386	    has_pprompt = "P-prompt" in succ
   387	
   388	    # F07 audit fix 2026-05-09: per-comparison universe — each oracle
   389	    # contrast uses ONLY the arms it compares, not a global intersection
   390	    # across all present modes. Previously a partial P-prompt arm could
   391	    # shrink the 3-vs-5 denominator even though P-prompt is not in that
   392	    # estimand. Universes:
   393	    #   universe_psom_only:    obs(DOM, SoM, Vision, P-SoM)
   394	    #   universe_pdom_only:    obs(DOM, SoM, Vision, P-text)
   395	    #   universe_pprompt_only: obs(DOM, SoM, Vision, P-prompt)
   396	    #   universe_5:            obs(DOM, SoM, Vision, P-text, P-SoM)   ← 3-vs-5 denominator
   397	    #   universe_6:            obs(DOM, SoM, Vision, P-text, P-SoM, P-prompt)
   398	    # `n_common` reported in the CSV = |universe_5| if P-text present,
   399	    # else |universe_psom_only| (closest match to historical semantics).
   400	
   401	    def _universe(arms: list) -> set:
   402	        return set.intersection(*[obs[a] for a in arms if a in obs])
   403	
   404	    universe_psom_only = _universe(["DOM", "SoM", "Vision", "P-SoM"])
   405	    universe_pdom_only = _universe(["DOM", "SoM", "Vision", "P-text"]) if has_pdom else set()
   406	    universe_pprompt_only = _universe(["DOM", "SoM", "Vision", "P-prompt"]) if has_pprompt else set()
   407	    if has_pdom:
   408	        universe_5 = _universe(["DOM", "SoM", "Vision", "P-text", "P-SoM"])
   409	    else:
   410	        universe_5 = universe_psom_only
   411	    if has_pdom and has_pprompt:
   412	        universe_6 = _universe(["DOM", "SoM", "Vision", "P-text", "P-SoM", "P-prompt"])
   413	    else:
   414	        universe_6 = set()
   415	
   416	    common = universe_5 if has_pdom else universe_psom_only
   417	    n = len(common)
   418	    if n < MIN_EP_FOR_CELL:
   419	        return None
   420	
   421	    # Restrict each mode's success set to its own comparison's universe
   422	    # at use site (not globally as before).
   423	    def _restrict_set(arms: list) -> tuple[set, dict]:
   424	        u = _universe(arms)
   425	        return u, {a: succ[a] & u for a in arms if a in succ}
   426	
   427	    # P-SoM only (3 → 4_psom)
   428	    u_psom, succ_r_psom = _restrict_set(["DOM", "SoM", "Vision", "P-SoM"])
   429	    union_3_psom_only = succ_r_psom["DOM"] | succ_r_psom["SoM"] | succ_r_psom["Vision"]
   430	    union_4_psom = union_3_psom_only | succ_r_psom["P-SoM"]
   431	    sr_3_psom_only = 100 * len(union_3_psom_only) / max(1, len(u_psom))
   432	    sr_4_psom = 100 * len(union_4_psom) / max(1, len(u_psom))
   433	    universe_psom = sorted(u_psom)
   434	    in_3_psom = np.array([t in union_3_psom_only for t in universe_psom], dtype=bool)
   435	    in_4_psom = np.array([t in union_4_psom for t in universe_psom], dtype=bool)
   436	
   437	    # CSV-reported sr_3 / union_3 use universe_5 (paper-grade primary
   438	    # denominator when P-text present; same as universe_psom otherwise).
   439	    succ_r = {m: s & common for m, s in succ.items()}
   440	    union_3 = succ_r["DOM"] | succ_r["SoM"] | succ_r["Vision"]
   441	    sr_3 = 100 * len(union_3) / n
   442	    universe = sorted(common)
   443	    # Backward-compat aliases for downstream 5-mode / H3 axis tests
   444	    # which use in_3 indexed against universe_5.
   445	    in_3 = np.array([t in union_3 for t in universe], dtype=bool)
   446	
   447	    # Single-P-SoM lift CI (uses P-SoM-specific universe per F07)
   448	    ci_lo_psom, ci_hi_psom = bootstrap_lift_ci(in_3_psom, in_4_psom)
   449	    h_4psom_vs_3 = cohen_h(sr_4_psom / 100, sr_3_psom_only / 100)
   450	    wstat_psom, wp_psom = wilcoxon_signed_rank(in_3_psom, in_4_psom)
   451	    mc_p_psom = mcnemar_exact_one_sided(in_3_psom, in_4_psom)
   452	    tost_p_psom = bootstrap_tost_p(in_3_psom, in_4_psom)
   453	
   454	    psom_adds = succ_r["P-SoM"] - union_3
   455	
   456	    if has_pdom:
   457	        union_4_pdom = union_3 | succ_r["P-text"]
   458	        union_5 = union_3 | succ_r["P-text"] | succ_r["P-SoM"]
   459	        sr_4_pdom = 100 * len(union_4_pdom) / n
   460	        sr_5 = 100 * len(union_5) / n
   461	        in_4_pdom = np.array([t in union_4_pdom for t in universe], dtype=bool)
   462	        in_5 = np.array([t in union_5 for t in universe], dtype=bool)
   463	        ci_lo, ci_hi = bootstrap_lift_ci(in_3, in_5)
   464	        ci_lo_pdom, ci_hi_pdom = bootstrap_lift_ci(in_3, in_4_pdom)
   465	        h_5_vs_3 = cohen_h(sr_5 / 100, sr_3 / 100)
   466	        h_4pdom_vs_3 = cohen_h(sr_4_pdom / 100, sr_3 / 100)
   467	        wstat_5, wp_5 = wilcoxon_signed_rank(in_3, in_5)
   468	        wstat_pdom, wp_pdom = wilcoxon_signed_rank(in_3, in_4_pdom)
   469	        mc_p_5 = mcnemar_exact_one_sided(in_3, in_5)
   470	        mc_p_pdom = mcnemar_exact_one_sided(in_3, in_4_pdom)
   471	        tost_p_5 = bootstrap_tost_p(in_3, in_5)
   472	        tost_p_pdom = bootstrap_tost_p(in_3, in_4_pdom)
   473	        pdom_adds = succ_r["P-text"] - union_3
   474	        both_add = pdom_adds & psom_adds
   475	        pdom_only = pdom_adds - psom_adds
   476	        psom_only = psom_adds - pdom_adds
   477	        inter = succ_r["P-SoM"] & succ_r["P-text"]
   478	        unionj = succ_r["P-SoM"] | succ_r["P-text"]
   479	        jaccard = (len(inter) / len(unionj)) if unionj else 0.0
   480	        jaccard_warn = jaccard > 0.7
   481	    else:
   482	        sr_4_pdom = None
   483	        sr_5 = None
   484	        ci_lo = ci_hi = None
   485	        ci_lo_pdom = ci_hi_pdom = None
   486	        h_5_vs_3 = None
   487	        h_4pdom_vs_3 = None
   488	        wp_5 = wp_pdom = None
   489	        mc_p_5 = mc_p_pdom = None
   490	        tost_p_5 = tost_p_pdom = None
   491	        pdom_adds = both_add = pdom_only = set()
   492	        psom_only = psom_adds  # no overlap with absent P-text
   493	        jaccard = None
   494	        jaccard_warn = False
   495	
   496	    # P-prompt 4-mode lift + 6-mode oracle (when present)
   497	    if has_pprompt:
   498	        # F07 audit fix 2026-05-09: P-prompt-only comparison uses
   499	        # universe_pprompt_only (DOM ∩ SoM ∩ Vision ∩ P-prompt), NOT the
   500	        # 5-mode universe — otherwise the denominator drops by tasks
   501	        # missing in P-text/P-SoM that have nothing to do with this arm.
   502	        u_pprompt, succ_r_pprompt = _restrict_set(["DOM", "SoM", "Vision", "P-prompt"])
   503	        union_3_pprompt_only = succ_r_pprompt["DOM"] | succ_r_pprompt["SoM"] | succ_r_pprompt["Vision"]
   504	        union_4_pprompt = union_3_pprompt_only | succ_r_pprompt["P-prompt"]
   505	        sr_3_pprompt_only = 100 * len(union_3_pprompt_only) / max(1, len(u_pprompt))
   506	        sr_4_pprompt = 100 * len(union_4_pprompt) / max(1, len(u_pprompt))
   507	        u_pprompt_sorted = sorted(u_pprompt)
   508	        in_3_pprompt = np.array([t in union_3_pprompt_only for t in u_pprompt_sorted], dtype=bool)
   509	        in_4_pprompt = np.array([t in union_4_pprompt for t in u_pprompt_sorted], dtype=bool)
   510	        ci_lo_pprompt, ci_hi_pprompt = bootstrap_lift_ci(in_3_pprompt, in_4_pprompt)
   511	        h_4pprompt_vs_3 = cohen_h(sr_4_pprompt / 100, sr_3_pprompt_only / 100)
   512	        wstat_pprompt, wp_pprompt = wilcoxon_signed_rank(in_3_pprompt, in_4_pprompt)
   513	        mc_p_pprompt = mcnemar_exact_one_sided(in_3_pprompt, in_4_pprompt)

   520	            # universe_5 which can include tasks where P-prompt was

   565	    # H3 structural test: phantom space 2-axis empirical validation.
